title: Joseph spares Mary public shame
summary: When Mary is found pregnant, Joseph, a righteous man, decides to divorce her quietly rather than expose her to public shame.

title: Follow Jesus and fish for people
summary: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him and promises to make them fishers of people.

title: The merciful receive mercy
summary: Those who show mercy to others are blessed and will themselves be shown mercy.

title: Blessed are the peacemakers
summary: Those who work to make peace are blessed and will be called sons of God.

title: Rejoice when persecuted for Jesus
summary: When you are insulted, persecuted, or falsely slandered because of Jesus, rejoice: you are blessed, your reward is great, and the prophets were treated the same.

title: Let your good deeds shine
summary: Disciples are salt and light; let your good deeds be seen by others so they glorify your Father in heaven.

title: Anger and contempt are serious
summary: Jesus extends the command against murder to anger at a brother and to contemptuous insults, which also bring judgment.

title: Reconcile before you worship
summary: If you remember at the altar that a brother has something against you, leave your gift, go and be reconciled first, then return to worship.

title: Settle quickly with your adversary
summary: Reconcile quickly with an opponent while still on the way to court, before he hands you to the judge and you end up in prison paying every penny.

title: Don't discard your wife
summary: Jesus tightens the divorce rule: divorcing a wife except for sexual immorality brings adultery upon her, and marrying a divorced woman is adultery.

title: Let your yes mean yes
summary: Don't swear oaths at all—by heaven, earth, Jerusalem, or your own head; simply let your yes mean yes and your no mean no.

title: Turn the other cheek
summary: Rather than eye-for-eye payback, don't resist an evil person: turn the other cheek, yield your cloak too, and go the second mile.

title: Give to those who ask
summary: Give to the one who asks of you, and don't turn away someone who wants to borrow.

title: Love your enemies
summary: Love your enemies and pray for your persecutors, like the Father who is good to all; loving or greeting only your own is what outsiders already do.

title: Give to the needy in secret
summary: Don't give to the needy to be seen and praised by people; give quietly, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

title: Forgiving others and being forgiven
summary: Disciples ask forgiveness as people who have forgiven their debtors; if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive you.

title: Remove your own beam first
summary: Don't judge, for you'll be judged by the same measure; deal with the beam in your own eye before removing the speck from your brother's.

title: Don't press holy things on scoffers
summary: Don't hand what is holy to dogs or throw pearls to pigs, who will trample them and turn on you; use discernment with people who scorn sacred things.

title: Treat others as you'd want
summary: In everything, do to others what you would want them to do to you; this sums up the Law and the Prophets.

title: Beware of false prophets
summary: Watch out for false prophets who look like sheep but are wolves; recognize them by the fruit their lives produce.

title: Jesus touches a leper
summary: When a man with leprosy asks to be made clean, Jesus reaches out, touches him, says he is willing, and heals him.

title: Jesus honors a centurion's faith
summary: Jesus readily agrees to go to a centurion's servant, praises the Gentile's faith above any in Israel, and foresees many from east and west at God's banquet.

title: Jesus eats with sinners
summary: Jesus calls a tax collector and dines with sinners; when Pharisees object, he says the sick need a doctor and God desires mercy, not sacrifice.

title: Pray for harvest workers
summary: Moved with compassion for harassed, shepherdless crowds, Jesus tells his disciples to ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers.

title: Proclaim, heal, and give freely
summary: Jesus sends the Twelve to Israel's lost sheep, not Gentiles or Samaritans, to announce the kingdom and heal; freely you have received, so freely give.

title: Travel light; bless welcoming homes
summary: Go without extra provisions, since workers deserve their keep; stay with a worthy household and let your greeting of peace rest on it.

title: Shake off the dust
summary: If a home or town won't welcome you or listen, shake the dust off your feet as you leave; that town will answer to God at judgment.

title: Shrewd and innocent among wolves
summary: Sent like sheep among wolves, be shrewd yet innocent; when hauled before councils and rulers, don't worry what to say—the Spirit will speak through you.

title: Endure hatred; flee persecution
summary: Expect betrayal even by family and hatred because of Jesus' name; persevere to the end, and when persecuted in one town, flee to the next.

title: Don't fear those who oppose you
summary: Disciples will be maligned like their master, but don't fear people who can only kill the body; proclaim openly, trusting the Father who values you.

title: Acknowledge Jesus before others
summary: Whoever openly acknowledges Jesus before people will be acknowledged before the Father; whoever denies him will be denied.

title: When faith divides a family
summary: Following Jesus may set family members against each other; love for parents or children must not outrank loyalty to him.

title: Welcome and help Christ's messengers
summary: Receiving Jesus' messengers is receiving him; even a cup of cold water given to a little one because he is a disciple will be rewarded.

title: A friend of tax collectors
summary: Critics call Jesus a glutton, a drunkard, and a friend of tax collectors and sinners because he eats and drinks with people; wisdom is proven right by its results.

title: Mercy keeps us from condemning
summary: When Pharisees condemn his hungry disciples for picking grain, Jesus says knowing God desires mercy, not sacrifice, would have kept them from condemning the innocent.

title: It is right to do good
summary: Challenged about healing on the Sabbath, Jesus says a person is worth far more than a sheep, so doing good is always lawful.

title: He will not quarrel
summary: When Pharisees plot against him, Jesus withdraws, fulfilling Isaiah's Servant who does not quarrel or shout and will not break a bruised reed.

title: Words reveal the heart
summary: The mouth speaks from what fills the heart; everyone will give account on judgment day for every careless word, and words will acquit or condemn.

title: Jesus' true family
summary: Told his mother and brothers are outside, Jesus points to his disciples: whoever does the Father's will is his brother, sister, and mother.

title: Rejected in his hometown
summary: Jesus' hometown takes offense at him; he says a prophet lacks honor only at home and among his own household, and does few miracles there because of their unbelief.

title: John confronts Herod's sin
summary: John the Baptist keeps telling Herod that taking his brother's wife is unlawful, and is imprisoned for speaking the truth to a ruler.

title: Feed the hungry crowd yourselves
summary: Moved with compassion, Jesus heals the crowd's sick, and when the disciples want to send the hungry people away, he tells them to feed the crowd themselves.

title: Don't dodge caring for parents
summary: Jesus condemns using a religious vow as an excuse to stop supporting one's father and mother, saying it cancels God's command to honor parents.

title: Leave the blind guides alone
summary: Told the Pharisees were offended by his teaching, Jesus says to disregard them: they are blind guides, and blind leaders and followers both fall into a pit.

title: Jesus answers a Canaanite mother
summary: A Canaanite woman keeps pleading for her daughter despite Jesus' silence, the disciples' impatience and his hard saying; he praises her great faith and heals the girl.

title: Compassion for a hungry crowd
summary: Jesus has compassion on a crowd that has been with him three days without food and refuses to send them away hungry.

title: Pay so as not to offend
summary: Though they are exempt, Jesus has Peter pay the temple tax for both of them so as not to cause offense, giving up a right for others' sake.

title: Humble like a little child
summary: Asked who is greatest, Jesus sets a child among them: whoever humbles himself like this child is greatest, and welcoming such a child in his name welcomes him.

title: Don't cause others to stumble
summary: A warning: whoever causes a believing little one to stumble would be better drowned with a millstone; woe to the one through whom stumbling blocks come.

title: Seek the one who strays
summary: Don't look down on these little ones; like a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine to find one stray, the Father does not want any of them to perish.

title: Go to them privately first
summary: Confront a brother who sins against you privately to win him back; if he won't listen, bring one or two witnesses, then the church, then treat him as an outsider.

title: Agreement, prayer, and Jesus' presence
summary: Following the steps for confronting sin: heaven ratifies what disciples bind or loose, the Father answers agreeing prayer, and Jesus is with two or three gathered in his name.

title: Forgive seventy-seven times
summary: Peter asks whether forgiving a brother who sins against him seven times is enough; Jesus answers, not seven but seventy-seven times.

title: The unforgiving servant
summary: A servant forgiven an unpayable debt throttles a fellow servant over a small one; the master condemns him—so will the Father treat those who don't forgive from the heart.

title: What God joined, don't separate
summary: Jesus roots marriage in creation—two become one flesh, so let no one separate them; Moses permitted divorce for hard hearts, but divorce and remarriage except for immorality is adultery.

title: Let the children come
summary: When the disciples rebuke people for bringing little children, Jesus overrules them, welcomes the children, and lays hands on them: the kingdom belongs to such as these.

title: Sell and give to the poor
summary: A warning: a rich young man who claims to have kept the commandments, including neighbor-love, leaves sad when told to sell his possessions and give to the poor.

title: Leaving family for Jesus' sake
summary: Anyone who has left home, family or land for Jesus' sake will receive a hundred times as much and eternal life, an encouragement when faith costs family ties.

title: Don't resent another's generous reward
summary: In a parable of God's grace, all-day workers grumble when latecomers get equal pay, and the owner asks whether they resent his generosity; a warning against resentful comparison.

title: Seeking top seats breeds resentment
summary: A warning: the mother of Zebedee's sons asks Jesus for the top seats for them, and the other ten become indignant with the two brothers.

title: Greatness means serving
summary: Unlike Gentile rulers who lord it over people, whoever would be great among you must serve, as the Son of Man came to serve and give his life.

title: Jesus stops for the overlooked
summary: When the crowd tells two blind men to be quiet, Jesus stops, asks what they want, and, moved with compassion, heals them.

title: Invite everyone to the banquet
summary: When the invited guests refuse, the king sends servants to the street corners to invite everyone they find, bad and good alike, until the hall is full.

title: Give Caesar what is Caesar's
summary: Asked whether to pay taxes to Caesar, Jesus exposes the trap and answers: give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.

title: Love your neighbor as yourself
summary: Asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus names loving God and, second and like it, loving your neighbor as yourself; all the Law and Prophets hang on these.

title: Leaders who won't lift a finger
summary: Do what the scribes and Pharisees in Moses' seat tell you, but not what they do: they don't practice what they preach and load others with burdens they won't lift.

title: No titles—serve as brothers
summary: Unlike leaders who act for show and crave honored seats and titles, don't seek titles—you are all brothers; the greatest is your servant, and the self-exalting are humbled.

title: Don't neglect justice and mercy
summary: A warning: leaders who meticulously tithe herbs but neglect the law's weightier matters—justice, mercy, and faithfulness—should have practiced these without neglecting the others.

title: Jesus grieves over those rejecting him
summary: Jesus laments that Jerusalem kills the prophets, though he often longed to gather its people as a hen gathers her chicks; they were unwilling.

title: When persecution makes love grow cold
summary: A warning: disciples will be hated by all nations for Jesus' name; many will betray and hate one another as love grows cold, but persevere to the end.

title: Care for those in your charge
summary: The faithful servant feeds the household on time while his master is away; the wicked one beats his fellow servants and carouses, and is punished when the master returns.

title: Serving the least serves Christ
summary: At the judgment the King counts feeding the hungry, welcoming strangers, clothing the naked, and visiting the sick and imprisoned as done to him—and neglecting them as neglecting him.

title: Jesus defends a criticized woman
summary: When the disciples indignantly call a woman's costly anointing a waste that could have gone to the poor, Jesus rebukes them for troubling her and praises her beautiful deed.

title: Put your sword away
summary: When a companion slashes the high priest's servant during Jesus' arrest, Jesus orders him to put away the sword: all who draw the sword will die by it.

title: Silent before false accusers
summary: When false witnesses testify against him before the Sanhedrin, Jesus stays silent and offers no defense, speaking only when the high priest puts him under oath.

title: Peter denies knowing Jesus
summary: A warning: questioned by servant girls and bystanders, Peter three times denies knowing Jesus, finally with curses and oaths, then weeps bitterly.

title: Jesus' restraint before Pilate
summary: Before the governor, Jesus answers Pilate's question briefly but makes no reply to any of the chief priests' many accusations, to Pilate's amazement.

title: Make disciples of all nations
summary: With all authority given to him, Jesus sends his disciples to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to obey everything he commanded, promising his presence.

title: Follow Jesus and fish for people
summary: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him and promises to make them fishers of people.

title: Jesus touches a leper
summary: Moved with compassion, Jesus reaches out and touches a man with leprosy who begs to be made clean, and heals him.

title: Friends carry a friend to Jesus
summary: Four men carry their paralyzed friend to Jesus, dig through a roof to lower him down, and Jesus responds to their faith.

title: Jesus eats with sinners
summary: Jesus calls Levi the tax collector and eats with many tax collectors and sinners; to the scribes' objection he says the sick, not the healthy, need a doctor.

title: Choose to do good
summary: Watched by accusers, Jesus asks whether the Sabbath is for doing good or evil, saving life or destroying it; grieved and angered by their hard hearts, he heals.

title: Jesus' true family
summary: With his family outside—they had thought him out of his mind—Jesus looks at those around him: whoever does God's will is his brother, sister, and mother.

title: Go home and tell your people
summary: Jesus declines the healed man's request to come along, sending him home to tell his own people how much the Lord has done for him.

title: Jesus stops for a suffering woman
summary: Jesus stops for a woman who touched him in the crowd, listens to her whole story, calls her daughter, and sends her away in peace.

title: Rejected by his own
summary: Jesus' hometown and relatives take offense at him; a prophet lacks honor among his own, yet after marveling at their unbelief he goes on teaching village to village.

title: Sent out two by two
summary: Jesus sends the Twelve out two by two, traveling light and staying where welcomed; if a place rejects them, they shake off its dust as a testimony.

title: The Twelve preach and heal
summary: The Twelve go out preaching that people should repent, driving out demons and anointing and healing many who are sick.

title: John confronts Herod's sin
summary: John keeps telling Herod that taking his brother's wife is unlawful; Herodias nurses a grudge, but Herod fears and protects John and listens to him gladly.

title: Jesus makes his team rest
summary: When the returning apostles are too busy even to eat, Jesus takes them away to a quiet place to rest, a leader caring for his team.

title: Feed the crowd yourselves
summary: Seeing a crowd like sheep without a shepherd, Jesus has compassion and teaches them, then tells disciples who want to send them away to feed them themselves.

title: Don't dodge caring for parents
summary: Jesus condemns declaring money owed to parents an offering to God, which leaves them without help and cancels God's command to honor father and mother.

title: Jesus answers a Gentile mother
summary: Near Tyre, a Gentile woman of Syrophoenician birth keeps begging Jesus to free her daughter; because of her reply to his hard saying, he frees the girl.

title: Compassion for a hungry crowd
summary: Jesus has compassion on a crowd three days without food, some from far away, and refuses to send them home hungry.

title: Don't be ashamed of Jesus
summary: Don't be ashamed of Jesus and his words before this sinful generation; the Son of Man will be ashamed of whoever is ashamed of him.

title: Last of all, servant of all
summary: When the disciples argue over who is greatest, Jesus says whoever wants to be first must be last and servant of all, and welcoming a little child welcomes him.

title: Don't stop those outside your group
summary: John tried to stop a man driving out demons in Jesus' name because he didn't follow with them; Jesus says don't stop him—whoever is not against us is for us.

title: Even a cup of water counts
summary: Anyone who gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ will never lose his reward.

title: Don't cause others to stumble
summary: A warning: whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Jesus to stumble would be better off thrown into the sea with a millstone around his neck.

title: Be at peace with one another
summary: Have salt among yourselves and be at peace with one another—Jesus' closing word to disciples who had argued over which of them was the greatest.

title: What God joined, don't separate
summary: Jesus roots marriage in creation—the two become one flesh, so let no one separate them—and tells the disciples that divorcing and remarrying is adultery, for husband or wife.

title: Let the children come
summary: Indignant when the disciples rebuke those bringing children, Jesus welcomes them, takes them in his arms, and blesses them; the kingdom must be received like a child.

title: Sell and give to the poor
summary: A warning: a rich man who claims to keep the commandments, including not cheating others, leaves sad when Jesus, loving him, tells him to sell everything and give to the poor.

title: Leaving family for Jesus' sake
summary: Whoever leaves home and family for Jesus and the gospel receives a hundredfold now in homes and family, along with persecutions, and eternal life to come.

title: Seeking top seats breeds resentment
summary: A warning: James and John ask Jesus for the seats at his right and left in his glory, and the other ten become indignant with them.

title: Greatness means serving
summary: Unlike Gentile rulers who lord it over others, whoever would be great must serve and be slave of all, as the Son of Man came to serve.

title: Jesus stops for the overlooked
summary: When many tell blind Bartimaeus to be quiet, Jesus stops, has him called over, and asks what he wants before healing him.

title: Forgive before you pray
summary: When you stand to pray, if you hold anything against anyone, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses too.

title: Give Caesar what is Caesar's
summary: Pressed by Pharisees and Herodians to say whether to pay taxes to Caesar, Jesus sees through the trap: give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.

title: Love your neighbor as yourself
summary: Jesus names loving God and loving your neighbor as yourself the greatest commands; a scribe agrees these outweigh all offerings and sacrifices and is told he is near the kingdom.

title: Beware leaders who seek status
summary: Watch out for scribes who parade in long robes, crave greetings and the best seats, defraud widows of their houses, and pray long for show; they face greater condemnation.

title: A poor widow gives everything
summary: Jesus points out a poor widow whose two small coins outgave all the rich donors, since she gave everything she had to live on.

title: Witness before councils and kings
summary: Expect councils, beatings, and trials before governors and kings as witnesses to them; when arrested, don't worry what to say—speak what you're given, for the Holy Spirit speaks.

title: Endure even family betrayal
summary: Brother will betray brother and children their parents to death; you will be hated by everyone because of Jesus' name, but whoever perseveres to the end will be saved.

title: Jesus defends a criticized woman
summary: When some scold a woman for wasting costly perfume on him, Jesus tells them to leave her alone; she did a beautiful thing, and they can help the poor anytime.

title: Silent before false accusers
summary: As false witnesses give inconsistent testimony against him, Jesus stays silent, answering only when the high priest asks directly whether he is the Christ.

title: Peter denies knowing Jesus
summary: A warning: confronted by a servant girl and bystanders, Peter three times denies knowing Jesus, finally with curses and oaths, then breaks down and weeps.

title: Jesus' restraint before Pilate
summary: Before Pilate, Jesus answers the governor's question briefly but makes no reply to the chief priests' many accusations, to Pilate's amazement.

title: Preach the gospel to everyone
summary: The risen Jesus sends his disciples into all the world to preach the gospel to every creature.
note: Mark 16:9–20 is missing from some of the earliest manuscripts; the ESV prints it in brackets.

title: Shepherds tell others about Jesus
summary: After finding the newborn just as the angel described, the shepherds tell others what they had been told about him, and their listeners marvel.

title: Jesus submits to his parents
summary: Though he had said he must be in his Father's house, the twelve-year-old Jesus returns to Nazareth with his parents and obeys them.

title: Share extra clothes and food
summary: Asked how to show repentance, John tells the crowds that anyone with an extra garment should give it to someone lacking one, and should share food the same way.

title: Be honest and fair at work
summary: John tells tax collectors to charge no more than required, and soldiers not to extort money or make false charges, but to be satisfied with their pay.

title: John confronts Herod's sin
summary: John rebukes Herod the ruler over Herodias, his brother's wife, and his many other wrongs; Herod responds by jailing John.

title: Good news for the poor
summary: Reading Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus describes his mission: announcing good news for the poor, freedom for prisoners, sight for the blind, and release for the oppressed.

title: Hometown fury over grace to outsiders
summary: When Jesus says prophets go unwelcome at home and recalls God's prophets helping a foreign widow and a Syrian leper, his hometown tries to kill him; he walks away.

title: Called to catch people
summary: Simon, overwhelmed by the catch, confesses he is a sinner; Jesus says not to fear, for he will now catch people, and the fishermen leave all to follow him.

title: Jesus touches a leper
summary: A man with advanced leprosy begs Jesus to cleanse him; Jesus touches him, says he is willing, and the disease leaves him at once.

title: Bringing a paralyzed man to Jesus
summary: Unable to get through the crowd, men lower a paralyzed man through the roof to Jesus, and Jesus responds to their faith.

title: Jesus eats with sinners
summary: Levi follows Jesus and throws a big dinner for tax collectors; when Pharisees object, Jesus says the sick need a doctor and he came to bring sinners to repentance.

title: Do good even under scrutiny
summary: With critics watching for grounds to accuse him, Jesus asks whether the Sabbath is for doing good or harm, saving life or destroying it, and heals a man's withered hand.

title: Rejoice when hated for Jesus
summary: Jesus calls his followers blessed when hated, shunned, and scorned for his sake; they should celebrate, because their heavenly reward is great and prophets were mistreated likewise.

title: Beware of everyone's approval
summary: Jesus warns that being praised by everyone is a danger sign, since people's ancestors spoke well of the false prophets too.

title: Love and bless your enemies
summary: Jesus tells his followers to love their enemies: do good to people who hate them, answer curses with blessing, and pray for their abusers.

title: Turn the other cheek
summary: Jesus says that when someone hits you on the cheek, offer the other one too, and if your coat is taken, let your shirt go as well.

title: Give without demanding it back
summary: Jesus tells his followers to give to whoever asks them and not to insist on recovering what someone takes from them.

title: Treat others as you'd want
summary: Jesus tells his followers to treat other people the way they would want to be treated themselves.

title: Love beyond those who love you
summary: Jesus says even sinners return kindness; his followers should love enemies, lend without expecting repayment, and be merciful like God, who is kind even to the ungrateful.

title: Don't judge; forgive and give
summary: Jesus says to stop judging and condemning others and to forgive and give generously, because the standard you use with others will be applied to you.

title: Remove your own log first
summary: Jesus warns that the blind can't guide the blind: before correcting a brother's small fault, first deal with the far bigger fault in your own life.

title: Words reveal the heart
summary: Jesus teaches that what people say reveals their hearts: good or evil words flow out of whatever a person has stored up inside.

title: Jesus honors a centurion's faith
summary: Jewish elders plead for a Gentile centurion who loves their people; Jesus sets out to heal his servant, then praises the officer's humble faith above any in Israel.

title: Compassion for a grieving widow
summary: Meeting a funeral procession for a widow's only son, Jesus feels compassion for her, tells her not to cry, raises the young man, and restores him to his grieving mother.

title: A friend of tax collectors
summary: Critics call austere John demon-possessed, then mock Jesus for feasting and keeping company with tax collectors and sinners; yet wisdom is proven right by those who follow it.

title: Jesus receives a sinful woman
summary: At a Pharisee's dinner, Jesus accepts a sinful woman's tearful devotion and, with a story of forgiven debts, corrects his host's silent contempt and neglected hospitality.

title: Women provide for Jesus' mission
summary: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many other women whom Jesus had healed travel with him and the Twelve, providing for them from their own funds.

title: Jesus' true family
summary: When his mother and brothers can't reach him through the crowd, Jesus says his true family is everyone who listens to God's word and puts it into practice.

title: Go home and tell your story
summary: When the frightened locals ask Jesus to leave, he goes, but sends the freed man, who wants to come along, home to tell what God did for him.

title: Jesus stops for a suffering woman
summary: On his way to a dying girl, Jesus stops for the chronically ill woman who touched him, hears her story, and calls her daughter, sending her away in peace.

title: Sent out to preach and heal
summary: Jesus sends the Twelve to proclaim God's kingdom and heal, traveling light and staying where welcomed, and, where refused, to shake that town's dust from their feet.

title: Feed the hungry crowd yourselves
summary: Jesus welcomes the crowds who follow him to a remote place; when the Twelve want them sent off to find food, he tells the disciples to provide it themselves.

title: Don't be ashamed of Jesus
summary: Jesus warns that whoever is embarrassed by him and his teaching will find the Son of Man embarrassed by them when he returns in glory.

title: Stop competing to be greatest
summary: When the disciples argue about rank, Jesus stands a child beside him: welcoming a child in his name welcomes him, and the least among them is greatest.

title: Don't stop those outside your group
summary: John tried to stop someone outside their group casting out demons in Jesus' name; Jesus says to leave him alone, since whoever isn't opposing you is on your side.

title: No revenge on an unwelcoming village
summary: A warning: when a Samaritan village won't receive Jesus because he is headed to Jerusalem, James and John want to destroy it with fire; Jesus rebukes them and moves on.

title: Sent ahead in pairs
summary: Jesus sends seventy-two followers ahead in pairs, tells them to pray for more workers for the plentiful harvest, and warns they go as vulnerable as lambs among wolves.

title: Offer peace and accept hospitality
summary: Jesus tells them to travel light, bless each home with peace, stay put and eat what hosts serve, since workers earn their keep, heal the sick, and announce God's kingdom.

title: When a town turns you away
summary: If a town rejects his messengers, they wipe off its dust as a sign against it yet still declare God's kingdom near; that town will fare worse than Sodom.

title: Rejecting you means rejecting Jesus
summary: Jesus tells his messengers that people's response to them is their response to him: rejecting them means rejecting him and the God who sent him.

title: Love God and your neighbor
summary: Asked how to gain eternal life, Jesus lets a law expert answer from Scripture: love God completely and your neighbor as you love yourself; doing this brings life.

title: The good Samaritan
summary: Jesus tells of a Samaritan who stops to care for a beaten traveler after a priest and Levite pass by, and urges his questioner to be that kind of neighbor.

title: Martha complains about her sister
summary: Martha, busy hosting, complains to Jesus that her sister isn't helping; Jesus gently names her anxiety and defends Mary's choice to sit and listen to him.

title: Forgive as you seek forgiveness
summary: In the prayer Jesus teaches, his followers ask God's forgiveness while affirming that they too forgive everyone who wrongs them.

title: Give from the heart, not greed
summary: Jesus tells a Pharisee host, surprised that he skipped ritual washing, that inner greed is the real problem and giving to the poor from within makes everything clean.

title: Don't neglect justice and love
summary: A warning: Jesus condemns Pharisees who carefully tithe garden herbs yet ignore justice and love for God; they should have done these while still tithing.

title: Don't crave honor and status
summary: A warning: Jesus rebukes Pharisees who love the prominent seats at the synagogue and being greeted with deference in public.

title: Don't load burdens without helping
summary: A warning: when a law expert feels insulted, Jesus still rebukes teachers who load people with heavy burdens yet do nothing themselves to help carry them.

title: Fear God, not your persecutors
summary: Jesus tells his friends not to fear people who can only kill the body; fear God instead, who cares for even sparrows and values them far more.

title: Acknowledge Jesus before others
summary: Whoever openly acknowledges Jesus before people will be acknowledged before God's angels, but whoever disowns him before others will be disowned.

title: Don't fret over your defense
summary: When disciples are dragged before synagogues, rulers, and officials, they shouldn't worry about planning their defense; in that moment the Holy Spirit will give them the words.

title: Greed behind an inheritance dispute
summary: Asked to make someone's brother split an inheritance with him, Jesus declines to arbitrate between them and warns against all greed, since life isn't measured by possessions.

title: Generosity builds treasure in heaven
summary: Jesus tells his disciples to sell what they own and give to those in need, storing up lasting treasure in heaven, because the heart follows wherever one's treasure is.

title: Care for those in your charge
summary: Answering Peter, Jesus contrasts a manager who faithfully feeds the household in his master's absence with one who beats the servants and gets drunk, only to be punished severely.

title: When faith divides a family
summary: Jesus warns that he brings division rather than peace: households will split over him, setting fathers and sons, mothers and daughters, and in-laws against each other.

title: Settle with your opponent before court
summary: Use good sense and do all you can to settle with an opponent on the way to court, or the judge may jail you until you've paid every last cent.

title: Don't blame victims of tragedy
summary: Jesus denies that Galileans killed by Pilate or people crushed by a tower were worse sinners than others, and calls his hearers to repent themselves.

title: Jesus defends freeing a disabled woman
summary: When a synagogue leader objects to a Sabbath healing, Jesus says people water their animals on the Sabbath, so surely a woman bound for eighteen years should be set free.

title: Undeterred by a ruler's threat
summary: Told that Herod wants to kill him, Jesus refuses to be intimidated and sends word that he will keep healing and driving out demons until his work is done.

title: Jesus grieves over those rejecting him
summary: Jesus grieves that Jerusalem kills prophets and stones God's messengers, though he often wanted to shelter its people like a hen with her chicks, and they refused.

title: Doing good on the Sabbath
summary: At a Pharisee's meal Jesus heals a man with swelling and asks who wouldn't pull a son or an ox out of a well on the Sabbath.

title: Take the lowest seat
summary: Noticing guests grab the best seats, Jesus advises taking the lowest place and letting the host move you up, for self-promoters will be humbled and the humble lifted up.

title: Invite those who can't repay
summary: Jesus tells his host to invite the poor, disabled, and blind rather than friends, relatives, or rich neighbors who could return the favor; the reward comes at the resurrection.

title: Bring in the poor and outsiders
summary: When invited guests make excuses, a banquet host sends his servant to bring in the poor, disabled, and blind, then people from the country roads, until his house is full.

title: Jesus above every family tie
summary: In stark language, Jesus says no one can be his disciple who does not hate parents, spouse, children, siblings, and even his own life, and carry his own cross.

title: Jesus shares meals with sinners
summary: As tax collectors and sinners gather to hear Jesus, the Pharisees and scribes complain that he accepts such people and even eats with them, which prompts his three parables.

title: Seek the one who is lost
summary: Answering the complaint, Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one stray and calls friends to celebrate, as heaven rejoices over one repentant sinner.

title: Every lost one is worth finding
summary: A woman who loses one of ten coins searches her house until she finds it and calls neighbors to celebrate, like the joy among God's angels when a sinner repents.

title: A father welcomes his son home
summary: When a son who wasted his inheritance comes home repentant, his father sees him from far off, runs to embrace him, and restores him with a robe, ring, and feast.

title: The resentful older brother
summary: A warning: angry that years of dutiful service never earned him a party, the older son refuses to join the feast for his returned brother, despite his father's pleading.

title: Use money to gain friends
summary: After the parable of the shrewd manager, Jesus urges using worldly wealth to make friends, so they will welcome you into eternal homes.

title: Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus calls it adultery for a man to divorce his wife and marry someone else, and for a man to marry a woman who has been divorced.

title: Neglecting the beggar at your gate
summary: A warning: a rich man lives in luxury while the sick, hungry beggar Lazarus lies at his gate; after death their places reverse, and the rich man is in torment.

title: Don't cause others to stumble
summary: A warning: temptations to sin will certainly come, but whoever leads one of these little ones into sin would be better off drowned with a millstone around his neck.

title: Rebuke, then forgive every time
summary: Jesus says to correct a brother who sins and forgive him when he repents, even if he wrongs you seven times in a day and comes back repentant each time.

title: The grateful Samaritan outsider
summary: Of ten lepers Jesus cleanses, only one, a Samaritan, comes back to thank him and praise God; Jesus singles out this foreigner and commends his faith.

title: Humility, not contempt for others
summary: Told to those who trusted their own goodness and despised others: the tax collector pleading for mercy, not the Pharisee who scorns him, goes home right with God.

title: Don't keep children from Jesus
summary: When the disciples scold people for bringing babies to Jesus, he calls the children over and says not to block them, since God's kingdom belongs to people like them.

title: Sell and give to the poor
summary: A warning: a wealthy ruler who claims to have kept the commandments about treating others becomes very sad when Jesus tells him to sell everything and give to the poor.

title: Leaving family for the kingdom
summary: Anyone who has left home, spouse, siblings, parents or children for God's kingdom will receive far more now and eternal life in the age to come.

title: Jesus stops for the overlooked
summary: When people at the front tell a blind beggar to be quiet, Jesus stops, has him brought over, asks what he wants, and restores his sight.

title: Jesus goes home with Zacchaeus
summary: Jesus invites himself to stay with Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector; amid the crowd's grumbling, Zacchaeus pledges half his goods to the poor and fourfold repayment to anyone he cheated.

title: Jesus weeps over a resistant city
summary: Approaching Jerusalem, Jesus weeps over the city that is rejecting him, grieving that it did not recognize the way to peace.

title: Caesar's coin and God's due
summary: Spies try to trap Jesus over taxes to Caesar; pointing to the emperor's image on a coin, he says to give the emperor and God what each is owed.

title: Beware leaders who seek status
summary: Jesus warns about scribes who parade in long robes, crave public honor and the best seats, cheat widows out of their homes, and pray long prayers to look pious.

title: A poor widow gives everything
summary: Jesus says a poor widow's two tiny coins outweigh the gifts of the rich, since she gave everything she had to live on.

title: Persecution as a chance to testify
summary: Disciples arrested and brought before kings and governors for Jesus' sake should see it as a chance to testify, not rehearse a defense; he will give them irrefutable wisdom.

title: Endure betrayal and hatred patiently
summary: Disciples will be betrayed by parents, siblings, relatives, and friends, hated by everyone because of Jesus, and some killed, yet by enduring they will secure their lives.

title: Greatness means serving
summary: When the disciples argue over rank, Jesus says that unlike domineering Gentile kings, their greatest must act like the youngest and their leader like a servant, as he himself serves.

title: Restored to strengthen others
summary: Jesus tells Simon that Satan wants to test the disciples but he has prayed for Simon's faith to hold; once restored, Simon must steady and support his fellow disciples.

title: Stop the sword, heal the opponent
summary: When a disciple swings a sword during Jesus' arrest and cuts off the high priest's servant's right ear, Jesus halts the fighting and touches the ear to heal it.

title: Peter denies knowing Jesus
summary: A warning: in the high priest's courtyard Peter three times denies knowing Jesus; when the rooster crows and the Lord looks at him, he goes out weeping.

title: Silent before Herod and accusers
summary: Herod questions Jesus at length while the chief priests accuse him, but Jesus stays silent, even as Herod and his soldiers mock him.

title: Jesus forgives those crucifying him
summary: As he is crucified and his clothes are divided by lot, Jesus asks the Father to forgive those putting him to death, because they act in ignorance.

title: Urging a stranger to stay
summary: As evening falls, two disciples urge a traveler they don't recognize to stay the night with them rather than go on alone.

title: Witnesses to every nation
summary: The risen Jesus says the call to repent and be forgiven will go out in his name to every nation, starting in Jerusalem, with his disciples as witnesses.

title: Andrew brings his brother to Jesus
summary: After a day with Jesus, Andrew first goes and finds his own brother Simon, tells him they have found the Messiah, and brings him to Jesus.

title: Answering a skeptic with an invitation
summary: Philip tells Nathanael they have found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about; when Nathanael scoffs at Nazareth, Philip doesn't argue but invites him to come see.

title: Glad when another's ministry grows
summary: When John the Baptist's disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, he refuses rivalry: what anyone has comes from heaven, and he rejoices as Jesus grows and he fades.

title: Jesus reaches across the Samaritan divide
summary: Though Jews shunned Samaritans, Jesus asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, offers her lasting life, speaks frankly about her relationships, answers her worship question, and reveals himself as Messiah.

title: She tells her town about Jesus
summary: Returning disciples are surprised Jesus is talking with a woman, while she leaves her water jar and urges her town to come see if he could be the Christ.

title: The harvest is ready now
summary: Jesus tells his disciples to open their eyes, because the fields are ready for harvest now; he sends them to reap where others labored, and planter and harvester celebrate together.

title: Samaritans welcome Jesus and believe
summary: Many Samaritans believe because of the woman's testimony; at their request Jesus stays with them two days, and many more believe once they hear him for themselves.

title: When your own family doesn't believe
summary: Jesus' unbelieving brothers press him to display his works in Judea; he resists their pressure, since his time hasn't come, noting the world hates him for exposing its evil.

title: Judge rightly, not by appearances
summary: Facing anger for healing a man on the Sabbath, Jesus points out they circumcise on the Sabbath themselves, and tells them to stop judging by surface appearances and judge fairly.

title: Give the accused a fair hearing
summary: When the Pharisees dismiss Jesus, Nicodemus reminds them their own law hears a man out before condemning him; they mock him rather than address the point.

title: Mercy for a woman caught sinning
summary: Leaders use a woman caught in adultery to trap Jesus; he invites the sinless to throw the first stone, her accusers leave, and he sends her off uncondemned to sin no more.
note: The earliest manuscripts don't include John 7:53–8:11; the ESV prints it in brackets.

title: Leaving your honor to God
summary: Called a Samaritan and demon-possessed, Jesus denies having a demon, says they dishonor him while he honors his Father, and leaves his glory to God, the Judge.

title: Don't assume suffering means sin
summary: When the disciples assume a man was born blind because he or his parents sinned, Jesus says neither sinned; this happened so God's works could be shown in him.

title: Parents silenced by fear
summary: A warning: fearing expulsion from the synagogue for confessing Jesus, the healed man's parents confirm only that he is their son born blind and leave him to answer alone.

title: Standing by your testimony under pressure
summary: Pressed by the Pharisees to call Jesus a sinner, the healed man holds to what he knows, reasons that Jesus must be from God, and is insulted and thrown out.

title: Jesus seeks out the outcast
summary: Hearing that the healed man has been thrown out, Jesus goes and finds him, reveals himself as the Son of Man, and the man believes and worships him.

title: The shepherd versus the hired hand
summary: Jesus, the good shepherd, lays down his life for the sheep, unlike a hired hand who doesn't care for them and runs when danger comes.

title: Jesus weeps with grieving friends
summary: Seeing Mary and the mourners with her weeping over Lazarus, Jesus is deeply moved and weeps too, and onlookers remark how much he loved his friend.

title: Jesus defends Mary's costly gift
summary: Judas, a thief feigning concern for the poor, criticizes Mary for pouring costly perfume on Jesus; Jesus tells him to let her be, since she saved it for his burial.

title: Secret believers who feared exclusion
summary: A warning: many leaders believed in Jesus but would not say so openly for fear of being put out of the synagogue, because they loved human approval more than God's.

title: Jesus washes his disciples' feet
summary: Knowing the Father had given him all authority, and with his betrayer at the table, Jesus rises from supper, ties on a towel, and washes his disciples' feet.

title: Follow his example of humble service
summary: Having washed their feet, Jesus, their Lord and Teacher, tells the disciples to do the same for one another; no servant outranks his master, and blessing comes from doing it.

title: Welcome those Jesus sends
summary: Whoever welcomes someone Jesus sends welcomes Jesus himself, and whoever welcomes Jesus welcomes the Father who sent him.

title: Love each other as Jesus loved
summary: Jesus gives his disciples a new command: love one another just as he has loved them, and that love will show everyone they are his disciples.

title: Love that lays down its life
summary: Jesus commands his friends to love each other as he has loved them; the highest love is giving up your life for your friends.

title: When the world hates you
summary: If the world hates you, remember it hated Jesus first; because he chose you out of the world, expect to be persecuted as he was, on account of his name.

title: Testify alongside the Spirit
summary: Jesus promises the Spirit will testify about him, and tells his disciples they must testify as well, since they have been with him from the start.

title: Forewarned about persecution
summary: Jesus warns that his followers will be expelled from synagogues and even killed by people thinking they serve God; he tells them now so their faith won't fail.

title: Courage amid the world's trouble
summary: Jesus tells his disciples they will face trouble in the world, but in him they can have peace and courage, because he has conquered the world.

title: Jesus prays for their oneness
summary: Leaving his followers in the world, Jesus asks the Father to protect them so they may be one, just as he and the Father are one.

title: Not of the world, yet sent
summary: The world hates Jesus' followers because they don't belong to it; he asks not for their removal but protection from the evil one, and sends them into the world.

title: Unity so the world believes
summary: Jesus prays that his disciples and all who later believe may be one, as he and the Father are, so the world will believe and know the Father sent him.

title: Jesus shields his disciples
summary: When the arresting party says they want Jesus of Nazareth, he identifies himself and tells them to let his disciples go, so none of those given to him is lost.

title: No swords in Jesus' defense
summary: A warning: Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant, but Jesus orders him to sheathe his sword, resolved to undergo what his Father has given him.

title: Peter's first denial
summary: A warning: let into the high priest's courtyard, Peter tells the servant girl at the door that he is not Jesus' disciple, then warms himself among the officers.

title: Jesus protests an unjust blow
summary: Before the high priest, Jesus says he has taught openly; when an officer slaps him, he asks him to point out the wrong or explain the blow.

title: Peter denies Jesus twice more
summary: A warning: questioned at the fire and by a relative of the man whose ear he cut off, Peter twice more denies being Jesus' disciple; then a rooster crows.

title: Jesus answers Pilate plainly
summary: Questioned by Pilate, Jesus explains his kingdom does not come from this world, which is why his servants are not fighting, and that he came to testify to the truth.

title: Rulers' authority comes from above
summary: When Pilate tells the silent Jesus he can free or crucify him, Jesus answers that Pilate's authority is given from above, and the one who handed him over is guiltier.

title: Jesus provides for his mother
summary: From the cross, Jesus entrusts his mother to the disciple he loved as her son, and from then on the disciple takes her into his own home.

title: Sent as Jesus was sent
summary: Greeting his fearful disciples with peace, the risen Jesus tells them that just as the Father sent him, so he is now sending them.

title: Jesus restores Peter
summary: Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves him, meets each yes with a charge to feed and tend his flock, foretells Peter's death, and calls him to follow.

title: Be My witnesses everywhere
summary: Jesus promised the Spirit's power and sent His followers to bear witness about Him from Jerusalem through Judea and Samaria to the ends of the earth.

title: Praying together with one accord
summary: After Jesus' ascension, the apostles, the women, Mary, and Jesus' brothers kept praying together with one mind.

title: Answering mockers with reason
summary: When some mocked the Spirit-filled believers as drunk, Peter stood with the Eleven and answered the crowd with plain reasoning before explaining what God was doing.

title: Urging the crowd to repent
summary: Peter told the crowd plainly that they had crucified Jesus; when they were deeply convicted, he urged them to repent and be baptized, and about three thousand responded.

title: The first church's shared life
summary: The new believers devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, shared meals and prayer, sold possessions to meet anyone's need, met daily with glad hearts, and enjoyed everyone's goodwill.

title: Giving a beggar what they had
summary: Peter and John look a lame beggar in the eye, give him what they have, healing in Jesus' name, and take his hand to lift him up.

title: Frank yet gracious with a crowd
summary: Peter refused credit for the healing, then spoke frankly yet graciously to the crowd—calling them brothers who had acted in ignorance—and urged them to repent and turn back.

title: Bold answers before the council
summary: Questioned by the rulers about a kindness done to a lame man, Peter, filled with the Spirit, boldly testified that Jesus had healed him; the council marveled at their boldness.

title: Listening to God over rulers
summary: Commanded never to speak or teach in Jesus' name, Peter and John asked the rulers to judge whether obeying them over God was right, and said they could not stop.

title: Praying for boldness under threats
summary: Hearing the council's threats, the believers prayed together with one accord, asking God to take note of the threats and give His servants boldness to keep speaking His word.

title: No needy among them
summary: The believers were united in heart and soul and treated their possessions as shared; owners sold property and gave the proceeds for distribution, so no one among them lacked.

title: Barnabas gives his field
summary: Joseph, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas, meaning Son of Encouragement, sold a field he owned and brought the money to the apostles for the common distribution.

title: Lying about a generous gift
summary: A warning: Ananias and Sapphira passed off part of their sale price as the whole; the money was theirs to keep, but they lied to God, and both died.

title: Together and respected by outsiders
summary: The believers kept meeting together in Solomon's Colonnade; outsiders held them in high regard though none dared join them, yet many more came to believe.

title: Obey God rather than men
summary: Charged with defying the council's order not to teach about Jesus, Peter and the apostles answered that they must obey God rather than people, and kept testifying as witnesses.

title: Rejoicing to suffer for the Name
summary: Flogged and ordered to stop speaking, the apostles left rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer disgrace for Jesus' name, and kept teaching daily in public and at home.

title: Resolving the widows' complaint
summary: When Greek-speaking believers complained that their widows were overlooked in the daily food distribution, the apostles had the whole church choose seven Spirit-filled men to handle it.

title: Answering opponents with Spirit-given wisdom
summary: When men from the Synagogue of the Freedmen began arguing with Stephen, they were no match for the Spirit-given wisdom of his answers.

title: Jealousy that sold a brother
summary: A warning: in Stephen's retelling, the patriarchs' jealousy led them to sell their brother Joseph into slavery, though God was with Joseph and rescued him.

title: Urging fighting brothers to reconcile
summary: In Stephen's retelling, Moses urges two fighting Israelites to stop wronging each other since they are brothers, but the one in the wrong pushes him away.

title: Stephen's blunt rebuke of the council
summary: On trial before a hostile council, Stephen ended his defense with a blunt charge that, like their fathers, they resisted the Holy Spirit and betrayed and murdered the Righteous One.

title: Forgiving those who kill you
summary: As he was being stoned, Stephen entrusted his spirit to Jesus, then knelt and cried out for the Lord not to hold this sin against his killers.

title: Scattered but still preaching
summary: When persecution scattered the Jerusalem church, devout men buried and mourned Stephen, and the scattered believers preached the word wherever they went.

title: Philip preaches in Samaria
summary: Philip went to a Samaritan city and proclaimed the Christ; the crowds listened closely, many were healed and freed, and there was great joy in that city.

title: Praying for new Samaritan believers
summary: Hearing that Samaritans had received God's word, the Jerusalem apostles sent Peter and John, who prayed for the new believers and laid hands on them to receive the Spirit.

title: Rebuking sin, urging repentance
summary: When the newly baptized Simon offered money for the power to give the Spirit, Peter sharply exposed his wrong heart yet urged him to repent and pray for forgiveness.

title: Preaching in Samaritan villages
summary: After testifying in Samaria, Peter and John preached the gospel in many Samaritan villages on their way back to Jerusalem.

title: Philip and the Ethiopian official
summary: Led by the Spirit, Philip ran up to an Ethiopian official, asked about what he was reading, sat with him, explained Jesus from that very Scripture, and baptized him.

title: Ananias welcomes Saul as brother
summary: Sent to Saul, Ananias raised concerns about the man who had harmed believers, but obeyed, laid hands on him, greeted him as a brother, and Saul stayed with the disciples.

title: Preaching Christ, then escaping a plot
summary: Newly converted, Saul proclaimed Jesus in the Damascus synagogues; when opponents plotted to kill him, his disciples lowered him through the wall in a basket.

title: Barnabas vouches for a feared convert
summary: When the Jerusalem disciples were afraid of Saul and doubted his conversion, Barnabas took him to the apostles, told his story, and Saul was received among them.

title: Brothers protect Saul from danger
summary: Saul debated the Grecian Jews, who tried to kill him; learning of it, the brothers took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

title: Dorcas's life of kindness and charity
summary: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was always busy with works of kindness and charity; when she died, weeping widows showed Peter the clothing she had made.

title: A centurion's gifts to the poor
summary: Cornelius, a God-fearing centurion, gave generously to the people and prayed regularly; an angel told him his prayers and gifts to the poor had been remembered by God.

title: Hosting a Gentile's messengers
summary: Still puzzling over his vision, Peter obeyed the Spirit's call to go with the Gentile messengers without hesitation, invited them in as his guests, and set out with them.

title: Entering a Gentile's home
summary: Raising Cornelius from bowing at his feet, Peter entered his home despite the custom against associating with foreigners, because God had shown him to call no one unclean.

title: God shows no favoritism
summary: Peter recognized that God does not show favoritism but welcomes people from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.

title: Preaching peace to Gentile listeners
summary: Peter started from what Cornelius's household already knew about Jesus, testified as an eyewitness to His life, death and resurrection, and offered forgiveness to everyone who believes.

title: Welcoming Gentiles as equals
summary: When the Spirit fell on the Gentiles just as on Jewish believers, Peter asked who could refuse them baptism, had them baptized, and was invited to stay a few days.

title: Explaining himself to critical brothers
summary: Criticized by Jewish believers for eating with uncircumcised men, Peter explained step by step what God had done; their objections were settled and they praised God for granting Gentiles repentance.

title: Sharing the gospel with Greeks
summary: Most scattered believers spoke only to Jews, but some men from Cyprus and Cyrene began telling Greeks in Antioch about Jesus, and many believed.

title: Barnabas encourages a new church
summary: Sent from Jerusalem to Antioch, where many Greeks had believed, Barnabas rejoiced at God's grace, urged them all to remain faithful, and brought Saul to teach alongside him.

title: Famine relief for distant believers
summary: When a famine was foretold, the Antioch disciples each gave according to their ability and sent relief to the believers in Judea through Barnabas and Saul.

title: Praying hard for an imprisoned brother
summary: While Herod held Peter in prison after executing James, the church kept praying fervently to God for him.

title: Sending out missionaries with prayer
summary: The Antioch church's prophets and teachers fasted and prayed, laid hands on Barnabas and Saul, and sent them off to the work the Spirit had called them to.

title: Rebuking a false prophet's opposition
summary: When the sorcerer and false prophet Elymas tried to turn the proconsul from the faith, Paul, filled with the Spirit, rebuked him; Elymas was struck blind and the proconsul believed.

title: Using an invitation to speak
summary: Invited to give a word of encouragement in the synagogue, Paul addressed both Israelites and God-fearing Gentiles and traced God's story through their Scriptures to Jesus.

title: Following up with eager listeners
summary: When listeners asked to hear more, Paul and Barnabas talked further with the many Jews and converts who followed them and urged them to continue in God's grace.

title: Turning to the Gentiles
summary: When some Jews, jealous of the crowds, blasphemously contradicted Paul, he and Barnabas boldly replied that since they rejected the message, they would turn to the Gentiles.

title: Shaking off the dust
summary: Driven out by stirred-up persecution, Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet in protest and moved on to Iconium, while the disciples were filled with joy.

title: Staying bold, then fleeing danger
summary: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas kept speaking boldly though opponents poisoned people's minds against the believers; when a plot to stone them arose, they fled and kept preaching elsewhere.

title: Refusing worship, pointing to God
summary: When a pagan crowd tried to sacrifice to them as gods, Paul and Barnabas insisted they were mere men and pointed to the living Creator who sends rain and harvests.

title: Stoned, then back into town
summary: Opponents from Antioch and Iconium won over the crowd and stoned Paul, leaving him for dead; as the disciples gathered around him, he got up and returned to the city.

title: Strengthening disciples and appointing elders
summary: Paul and Barnabas revisited the new churches, strengthening and encouraging the disciples to remain in the faith through hardships, and appointed elders for each church with prayer and fasting.

title: Taking a dispute to the elders
summary: After sharp debate with teachers insisting Gentile believers be circumcised to be saved, the church sent Paul and Barnabas to the Jerusalem apostles and elders, who met to consider it.

title: No distinction between us and them
summary: Peter argued that God gave Gentiles the Spirit just as He did Jewish believers, making no distinction, so the church should not burden them with an unbearable yoke.

title: Listening well, then deciding
summary: The assembly listened in silence to Barnabas and Paul; then James, drawing on Scripture, judged they should not trouble Gentile converts, only ask them to avoid a few practices.

title: Communicating the decision with care
summary: With the whole church agreeing, the leaders sent trusted men with a brotherly letter disavowing the unauthorized troublers and asking nothing beyond a few essential requirements.

title: Encouragement after the decision
summary: The Antioch church rejoiced at the letter's encouraging message, and Judas and Silas spoke at length to encourage and strengthen them before being sent back in peace.

title: Paul and Barnabas part ways
summary: Paul and Barnabas disagreed so sharply over taking Mark, who had deserted them earlier, that they parted; Barnabas sailed with Mark, and Paul, commended by the brothers, took Silas.

title: Timothy circumcised for others' sake
summary: Paul chose Timothy, whom the brothers spoke well of, and circumcised him out of consideration for the local Jews, who all knew his father was Greek.

title: Answering the call to Macedonia
summary: After a vision of a Macedonian man pleading for help, Paul and his companions set out at once, concluding God had called them to preach the gospel there.

title: Lydia hears and opens her home
summary: Paul's group sat and spoke with women at a riverside place of prayer; the Lord opened Lydia's heart, and once baptized she urged them to stay at her home.

title: Singing in prison after a beating
summary: Stripped, beaten with rods and locked in stocks after a mob attack, Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns at midnight while the other prisoners listened.

title: Loving the jailer who held them
summary: Rather than escape, Paul stopped his jailer from killing himself and shared the gospel with his household; the jailer washed their wounds and fed them in his home.

title: Insisting on lawful treatment
summary: Offered a quiet release, Paul insisted that the magistrates who had publicly beaten Roman citizens without trial come escort them out themselves; alarmed, the magistrates complied.

title: Encouraging the brothers before leaving
summary: Released from prison, Paul and Silas went to Lydia's house to see and encourage the believers before leaving the city.

title: Reasoning from the Scriptures
summary: Paul spent three Sabbaths reasoning from the Scriptures in the synagogue, explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise; some Jews and many God-fearing Greeks were persuaded.

title: Jason pays for his hospitality
summary: Jealous opponents raised a mob, raided Jason's house, and hauled him before officials for welcoming Paul and Silas; after he posted bond, the brothers sent them away by night.

title: Escorting a threatened brother away
summary: When agitators from Thessalonica stirred up the crowds in Berea, the brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast and escorted him all the way to Athens.

title: Engaging a city full of idols
summary: Distressed by Athens' idols, Paul reasoned in the synagogue and daily in the marketplace with whoever he met, and engaged philosophers who mocked him yet asked to hear his teaching.

title: Starting from their altar and poets
summary: At the Areopagus, Paul began with the Athenians' altar to an unknown god and quoted their poets, then proclaimed the Creator, called all to repent, and pointed to the resurrection.

title: Mixed responses to the message
summary: At the mention of resurrection some mocked, some wanted to hear more, and a few believed; Paul simply left the council, and some joined him.

title: Working alongside fellow tentmakers
summary: In Corinth, Paul stayed with Aquila and Priscilla, recently expelled from Rome, working with them at their shared trade of tentmaking while reasoning every Sabbath with Jews and Greeks.

title: Moving next door after rejection
summary: When opponents insulted him, Paul shook out his garments, declared himself innocent of their blood, and moved next door; the synagogue leader and many Corinthians then believed.

title: Keep speaking; do not be afraid
summary: In a night vision the Lord told Paul not to fear or fall silent but keep speaking, since He was with him; Paul stayed a year and a half teaching.

title: Revisiting to strengthen disciples
summary: After time in Antioch, Paul traveled from place to place through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

title: Taking a gifted teacher aside
summary: When Priscilla and Aquila heard the eloquent Apollos teaching boldly while knowing only John's baptism, they took him in privately and explained the way of God more accurately.

title: Letters of welcome for Apollos
summary: When Apollos moved to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote asking the disciples there to welcome him; he greatly helped believers and publicly refuted opponents from the Scriptures.

title: Withdrawing from public maligning
summary: After three months of persuasive synagogue teaching, when some hardened and publicly maligned the Way, Paul withdrew with the disciples to a lecture hall and taught daily for two years.

title: Confessing and renouncing openly
summary: Many new believers openly confess their former practices, and former sorcerers publicly burn their valuable magic books.

title: Heeding friends' warnings in a riot
summary: When a riot over lost idol business engulfed Ephesus, Paul wanted to face the crowd, but the disciples and friendly provincial officials urged him not to enter the theatre.

title: Giving outsiders no cause for complaint
summary: Calming the riot, Ephesus's city clerk pointed out that Paul's companions had neither robbed their temple nor blasphemed their goddess, though Paul had turned many from idols.

title: Encouraging disciples before departing
summary: After the uproar, Paul gathered and encouraged the disciples before leaving, then spoke many words of encouragement throughout Macedonia on his way to Greece.

title: Serving with humility and tears
summary: Paul reminded the Ephesian elders how he served humbly and tearfully amid plots, taught everything helpful publicly and house to house, and testified to Jews and Greeks alike.

title: Facing coming hardship with resolve
summary: Warned that chains and afflictions awaited him, Paul counted his life of no value compared with finishing his course and testifying to the good news of God's grace.

title: Declaring the whole will of God
summary: Paul could declare himself innocent of everyone's blood because he had not held back from teaching the Ephesians the whole will of God.

title: Shepherd and guard the flock
summary: Elders must watch over themselves and the flock, shepherd God's church, and stay alert, because savage wolves and distorters from within will try to draw away disciples.

title: Working hard to help the weak
summary: Paul coveted nothing and worked to supply himself and his companions, showing that hard work should help the weak, for Jesus said giving is more blessed than receiving.

title: A tearful, prayerful farewell
summary: Paul knelt and prayed with the Ephesian elders; they wept, embraced and kissed him, grieved they would not see him again, and walked him to the ship.

title: Whole families praying on the beach
summary: Tyre's disciples hosted Paul's group for a week; at parting, they and their wives and children walked them out of the city and knelt on the beach to pray.

title: Staying with believers along the way
summary: Traveling toward Jerusalem, Paul's group greeted the brothers at Ptolemais and stayed a day, then lodged at Caesarea in the home of Philip the evangelist.

title: Yielding after a loving disagreement
summary: After Agabus foretold Paul's arrest, his friends tearfully begged him not to go; Paul said he was ready to die for Jesus, and they yielded: the Lord's will be done.

title: Hosted and welcomed joyfully
summary: Disciples from Caesarea brought Paul's group to lodge with Mnason, an early disciple, and the brothers in Jerusalem welcomed them joyfully.

title: Defusing rumors to keep unity
summary: Hearing that Jewish believers thought he taught Jews to abandon Moses, Paul took the elders' advice and joined a purification rite to show the rumors were untrue.

title: Asking to address a hostile mob
summary: Just rescued from a mob that tried to kill him, Paul courteously asked the Roman commander for a word, corrected his mistaken identity, and asked permission to address the people.

title: Finding common ground with accusers
summary: Given permission, Paul addressed the hostile crowd in Hebrew as brothers and fathers, identified with their zeal for God, and admitted he had once persecuted the Way himself.

title: Leaving where testimony is refused
summary: Paul recounted how the Lord told him to leave Jerusalem quickly because people there would not accept his testimony, and sent him far away to the Gentiles instead.

title: Invoking legal rights under arrest
summary: About to be flogged for interrogation, Paul asked the centurion whether it was lawful to flog a Roman citizen without a trial, and the interrogators stepped back.

title: Not speaking evil of rulers
summary: Struck at the high priest's order, Paul retorted, calling him a whitewashed wall; told who he was, Paul acknowledged Scripture's command not to speak evil of a ruler.

title: Take courage and keep testifying
summary: The night after his hearing, the Lord stood near Paul and told him to take courage: as he had testified in Jerusalem, he must testify in Rome.

title: Reporting a murder plot to authorities
summary: When his nephew learned of a plot to ambush him, Paul had a centurion take the young man to the commander, who drew him aside and heard the warning.

title: Courteous defense, clear conscience
summary: Before Governor Felix, Paul answered the charges courteously and factually, openly confessed following the Way, and said he always strives for a clear conscience before God and people.

title: Bringing alms to his people
summary: Paul explained that after several years away he had returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to his people and to present offerings.

title: Friends allowed to meet his needs
summary: Felix kept Paul under guard but gave him some freedom and allowed his friends to take care of his needs.

title: Speaking hard truth to a governor
summary: Summoned to speak about faith in Christ, Paul spoke to Felix about righteousness, self-control and coming judgment until Felix grew afraid; Felix, hoping for a bribe, kept sending for him.

title: Accepting just judgment, appealing to Caesar
summary: Facing charges his accusers could not prove, Paul said he had wronged neither the Jews nor Caesar, would not refuse death if guilty, and appealed to Caesar.

title: Respectful address to a king
summary: Given permission to speak, Paul told King Agrippa he considered himself fortunate to make his defense before someone familiar with Jewish customs, and asked him to listen patiently.

title: Sent to open their eyes
summary: Jesus appointed Paul as a servant and witness, sending him to his own people and the Gentiles to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light.

title: Calling everyone to repent
summary: Obeying the vision, Paul urged Jews and then Gentiles to repent, turn to God and show it by their deeds, testifying to small and great alike.

title: Answering ridicule with respect
summary: When Festus shouted that he was insane, Paul respectfully answered that he spoke sober truth and wished all his hearers would become as he was, except for the chains.

title: Officials find nothing wrong
summary: After hearing Paul, the king and the governor agree he has done nothing to deserve death or prison, a mark of blameless conduct before outsiders.

title: Kind centurion, caring friends
summary: At Sidon the centurion Julius treated Paul with consideration, letting him visit his friends and receive their care.

title: Encouraging frightened shipmates
summary: Though his earlier warning had been ignored, Paul stood among the despairing men aboard, urged them to take courage, and openly shared God's promise that no lives would be lost.

title: Caring for shipmates' practical needs
summary: Before dawn Paul urged everyone aboard to eat for their survival, assured them none would be harmed, and gave thanks to God before them all; they were encouraged and ate.

title: Welcomed by island strangers
summary: Shipwrecked on Malta, Paul's company received extraordinary kindness from the islanders, who built a fire and welcomed them all out of the rain and cold.

title: Healing the host's sick father
summary: Publius, the island's chief official, hosted them for three days; Paul visited and prayed for his sick father and healed him, then cured other islanders, who supplied their needs.

title: Brothers travel out to meet Paul
summary: Believers at Puteoli invited Paul's group to stay a week, and Roman believers traveled far to meet him; seeing them, Paul was encouraged and thanked God.

title: No grudge against his nation
summary: In Rome, Paul called together the Jewish leaders, addressed them as brothers, and explained that though handed over as a prisoner, he had no charge to bring against his nation.

title: Persuading all day, then warning
summary: Paul spent a whole day persuading Rome's Jews from the Law and Prophets; when some refused, he quoted Isaiah's warning and declared salvation sent to the Gentiles.

title: Welcoming all who came
summary: For two years in his rented house, Paul welcomed everyone who came to see him and boldly, freely proclaimed God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.

title: Pray constantly for fellow believers
summary: Paul thanks God for the Romans' widely known faith and says he prays for them continually, modeling thankful, persistent prayer for other believers.

title: Strengthen each other's faith
summary: Paul longs to visit Rome to strengthen the believers there, expecting that sharing their faith will lift both him and them.

title: Owe the gospel to everyone
summary: Paul feels a debt to share the gospel with every kind of person, educated or not, Jew or Gentile, and is unashamed to do so.

title: Don't condemn what you also do
summary: Condemning others while doing the same things brings judgment on yourself; remember that God's patient goodness toward sinners is meant to draw them to repent.

title: Hypocrisy makes outsiders mock God
summary: A warning: teaching others the right way while ignoring it yourself leads people outside the faith to speak against God because of your behavior.

title: Grieve over unbelieving kin
summary: Paul voices unceasing anguish for his unbelieving countrymen, even wishing he could be cut off himself for their sake: a model of costly love for those outside the faith.

title: Pray for those who don't believe
summary: Paul says his deepest wish and his prayer are for his fellow Israelites to be saved, modeling prayerful longing for unbelievers close to us.

title: People need someone to tell them
summary: People cannot trust Christ without hearing about him, and cannot hear without a messenger who is sent; some will still reject the message.

title: Work to win his own people
summary: Paul throws himself into his ministry to Gentiles, hoping it will stir his own people to jealousy and that some of them will be saved.

title: Gentile believers must not boast
summary: Gentile believers are warned not to feel superior to Jews who did not believe, since Gentiles stand only by faith and could be cut off too.

title: Don't overrate yourself
summary: Paul tells each member of the church to assess themselves realistically, by the faith God has given, instead of inflating their own importance.

title: Many members, one body
summary: Believers are many members of one body in Christ, each with a different role, and each belongs to all the others.

title: Use your gifts for others
summary: Whatever gift God has given, whether prophesying, serving, teaching, encouraging, giving, leading, or showing mercy, each person is to use it for the body, with generosity, diligence, and cheer.

title: Love genuinely and honor others
summary: Love must be genuine, hating evil and holding to good; be affectionately devoted to fellow believers and compete to show each other honor.

title: Meet needs and open your home
summary: Believers are to share with fellow Christians who are in need and to make a habit of welcoming guests.

title: Respond to persecutors with blessing
summary: Believers are to wish good on those who persecute them rather than cursing them.

title: Share others' joys and sorrows
summary: Believers are to celebrate with those who are celebrating and grieve with those who are grieving.

title: Seek harmony, not pride
summary: Be of one mind with each other, drop arrogance and conceit, and gladly spend time with people of low standing.

title: Refuse to pay back wrongs
summary: Do not answer a wrong with another wrong; aim to do what everyone would recognize as honorable.

title: Pursue peace as far as possible
