summary: Make every effort, within your own power, to be at peace with all people.

title: Leave payback to God
summary: Do not take revenge; trust God to judge, feed and give water to your enemy in need, and defeat evil by doing good rather than being beaten by it.

title: Submit to governing authorities
summary: Everyone is to submit to the governing authorities, since their authority comes from God, and resisting them means opposing God's arrangement and inviting judgment.

title: Authorities punish wrong; do right
summary: Rulers reward good conduct and punish bad as God's servants, so do what is right; submit not only from fear of penalty but out of conscience.

title: Pay taxes, respect, and honor
summary: Pay what is due to each person: taxes and revenue, along with respect and honor, as the authorities serve God in their work.

title: Love sums up the commandments
summary: Owe nobody anything except love; loving your neighbor covers every commandment about how we treat others, because love never harms a neighbor.

title: Put away strife and jealousy
summary: Paul tells believers to drop strife and jealousy along with drunkenness and sexual sin, and to live decently as people of the daytime.

title: Welcome believers who see things differently
summary: Take in the believer whose conscience is more restrictive, without arguing over opinions; neither side should look down on or condemn the other, because God has welcomed that person.

title: Each answers to the Lord
summary: On matters like special days and foods, each person should be settled in their own mind and act to honor the Lord, since all belong to him.

title: We all answer to God
summary: Looking down on or condemning a fellow believer is out of place, because each of us will answer to God personally.

title: Stop judging, remove obstacles
summary: Let us quit passing verdicts on each other and instead decide never to place anything in a fellow believer's path that could trip them up.

title: Love limits your freedom
summary: If your food choices grieve a fellow believer, you are not acting in love; do not wreck someone Christ died for, or let your freedom be slandered.

title: Pursue peace and mutual building
summary: God's kingdom is about right living, harmony, and Spirit-given gladness rather than diet, so chase what makes for peace and builds each other up.

title: Give up freedoms that trip others
summary: Do not tear down God's work over a meal; it is better to give up meat or wine than to do anything that makes a fellow believer stumble.

title: Keep private convictions private
summary: On disputed matters, keep your convictions between yourself and God without imposing them, and don't act against your own conscience, since that is sin.

title: The strong bear with the weak
summary: Stronger believers should shoulder the failings of the weak instead of pleasing themselves, seeking a neighbor's good and growth, following Christ's example of enduring insult rather than seeking ease.

title: A prayer for harmony
summary: Paul prays that God, the source of steadiness and comfort, will give the believers a shared outlook toward each other so they can praise him together.

title: Welcome one another as Christ did
summary: Receive each other warmly, the way Christ received you, so that God is honored.

title: Jew and Gentile worship together
summary: Christ served the Jewish people and showed mercy to Gentiles, and Scripture pictures both praising God together, the ground for welcoming one another.

title: Believers can instruct each other
summary: Paul expresses confidence that the Roman Christians are good and knowledgeable enough to teach and counsel one another.

title: Take the gospel to the unreached
summary: Paul describes bringing Gentiles to obedience through speech and action, and his ambition to preach where Christ had never been mentioned instead of building on others' work.

title: Churches give to poor believers
summary: Churches in Macedonia and Achaia gladly gave to help needy believers in Jerusalem, seeing it as a debt owed since Gentiles had shared in the Jews' spiritual riches.

title: Paul asks the church to pray
summary: Paul asks the Romans to strive with him in prayer for rescue from the unbelievers in Judea and for his service to be well received by believers there.

title: Welcome and help Phoebe
summary: Paul commends Phoebe, a church servant, and asks the Romans to receive her in a way fitting for believers and to assist her with whatever she needs.

title: Honor Prisca and Aquila
summary: Paul greets his coworkers Prisca and Aquila, who put their lives in danger for him and host a church in their home, and he notes the Gentile churches' gratitude.

title: Affirm hard workers by name
summary: Paul greets and affirms believers by name, noting Mary's hard work, the shared imprisonment and standing of Andronicus and Junia, and others he calls beloved, approved, or fellow workers.

title: Greet households and fellow believers
summary: Paul keeps greeting named believers and whole households, commending the hard work of Tryphena, Tryphosa, and Persis and the motherly care Rufus's mother showed Paul.

title: Greet each other affectionately
summary: Believers are told to greet each other with a pure, affectionate gesture of fellowship, and Paul adds that all the churches of Christ send greetings.

title: Steer clear of divisive people
summary: Watch out for and avoid people who stir up division against the teaching you learned; they serve themselves and mislead the gullible, so be wise about good.

title: Gaius hosts Paul and the church
summary: Gaius is noted as having opened his home to Paul and to the whole church, an example of ongoing hospitality.

title: Thanking God for fellow believers
summary: Before addressing their problems, Paul tells the Corinthians he constantly thanks God for the grace and gifts given them and is confident they will be kept steady to the end.

title: Refuse to split into factions
summary: Hearing of quarrels, Paul urges believers to agree and stop forming rival camps around favorite leaders, since Christ isn't divided and no leader was crucified for them.

title: Sharing the gospel without showmanship
summary: Paul came to Corinth feeling weak and afraid, with no polished rhetoric, preaching only the crucified Christ so their faith would depend on God's power, not clever argument.

title: Jealousy and rivalry are immature
summary: Paul tells the church their envy, quarreling and rival loyalties to Paul and Apollos show they are still spiritually immature and living by merely human standards.

title: Leaders are co-workers, not rivals
summary: Paul and Apollos are merely servants with assigned tasks, one sowing, one watering, while God gives growth; they work as a team, and each gets wages for his own work.

title: Don't brag about favorite leaders
summary: Believers should stop bragging about which human leader they follow, since every leader, and everything else, is theirs, and they themselves are Christ's.

title: Leave final verdicts to the Lord
summary: View leaders as Christ's servants who must prove trustworthy; don't pass verdicts early, since the Lord will come and reveal hidden intentions, and then God will commend each as deserved.

title: Don't rank leaders out of pride
summary: Paul used himself and Apollos as examples so believers would stop proudly backing one leader against another; everything they have was a gift, so there's no room for bragging.

title: Bless when insulted, answer kindly
summary: Paul describes how the apostles respond to abuse: they answer insults with blessing, put up with mistreatment, and reply kindly to false accusations, even while treated as the world's garbage.

title: Correcting as a loving father
summary: Paul writes not to humiliate them but to correct them as a loving father; he urges them to follow his example and sends Timothy to remind them how he lives.

title: Coming with discipline or gentleness
summary: Some had grown proud, assuming Paul wouldn't come; he warns he'll test them and lets them choose whether he comes ready to punish or with love and gentleness.

title: Removing a member in open sin
summary: While a man lived with his father's wife, the church stayed proud; it should have mourned and, meeting in Jesus' name, put him out, aiming at his final salvation.

title: Tolerated sin affects the whole church
summary: Their boasting was wrong: tolerated sin spreads through a church like yeast through dough, so clear it out and live with integrity and honesty, not malice.

title: Separate from sinning believers, not outsiders
summary: Shunning immoral or greedy unbelievers would mean withdrawing from society; instead refuse fellowship, even shared meals, with a professing believer living that way, since the church judges insiders, God outsiders.

title: Settle disputes within the church
summary: Believers in a dispute with each other shouldn't take it before unbelieving judges; the church should have a wise member decide such matters instead of exposing believers' quarrels to outsiders.

title: Suffer loss rather than exploit others
summary: Lawsuits among believers mean defeat; better to suffer injustice or loss than to exploit your brothers, for wrongdoers won't share in God's kingdom, and you've been cleansed from that life.

title: Spouses meet each other's needs
summary: Husband and wife owe each other sexual intimacy, each having a claim on the other's body; don't withhold it except briefly, when both agree, for prayer, then resume.

title: Spouses shouldn't separate or divorce
summary: Passing on the Lord's command, Paul says a wife shouldn't leave her husband (if she does, she should stay single or reconcile) and a husband shouldn't divorce his wife.

title: Married to an unbeliever
summary: A believer whose unbelieving spouse wants to stay shouldn't divorce, as spouse and children are set apart; if the unbeliever leaves, allow it, since God wants His people at peace.

title: Slave or free, belonging to Christ
summary: Slaves who come to faith needn't fret, though they may take freedom if they can; slave or free, each belongs to the Lord and should live for him.

title: Remarry only a believer
summary: A wife stays married to her husband for his lifetime; if he dies she's free to remarry whom she chooses, but only a fellow believer.

title: Love matters more than knowledge
summary: On food offered to idols, knowledge can make people proud while love strengthens others; anyone who thinks he has it all figured out still has much to learn.

title: Don't trip up a weaker believer
summary: Don't let your freedom over idol food make a believer with an uneasy conscience fall; that wrongs Christ, who died for him, and Paul would sooner quit meat.

title: Provide for gospel workers
summary: Like soldiers, farmers and temple workers, gospel preachers may rightly be supported by those they serve, as the Lord directed, though Paul declined this so nothing would obstruct the gospel.

title: Adapting to reach different people
summary: Though free, Paul put himself at everyone's service, adapting to Jews, Gentiles and the weak while still obeying Christ, to bring as many people as he could to faith.

title: Don't join in pagan worship meals
summary: Idols are nothing, yet pagan sacrifices are offered to demons, so believers must not share in those ritual meals; taking part in the Lord's Supper rules out joining idol feasts.

title: Seek what benefits others
summary: Freedom isn't the only test: not everything allowed is helpful or builds others up, so each person should pursue what benefits others rather than himself.

title: Eating with unbelieving hosts
summary: You may accept an unbeliever's dinner invitation and eat what's served without probing; but if someone says the food was offered to idols, abstain for that person's conscience.

title: Don't be an obstacle to anyone
summary: Let everything you do honor God; avoid tripping up Jews, Greeks or the church; follow Paul, as he follows Christ, in seeking others' benefit so many may be saved.

title: Divisions at the Lord's Supper
summary: A warning: the Corinthians' gatherings were split, with some eating their own meals and getting drunk while others went hungry, shaming the have-nots and treating God's church with contempt.

title: Eat together, not ahead of others
summary: When gathering to eat the Lord's Supper, hold off until everyone can eat together, and satisfy hunger at home, so the gathering doesn't bring judgment.

title: Gifts are given to help others
summary: Believers receive differing gifts, kinds of service and activities, all from the same Spirit, Lord and God, and each person's gift is given to benefit everyone.

title: One body from every background
summary: Christ's people form one body with many parts: Jews and Greeks, slaves and free alike have been joined into it and share the same Spirit.

title: Every member belongs
summary: Members who feel different, like a foot or an ear, still belong to the body; God placed every part deliberately, and a one-part body wouldn't be a body.

title: Honor and care for every member
summary: No member can call another unnecessary; weaker-seeming members are vital and honored, so the body stays undivided, with members caring for each other and sharing pain and joy.

title: Without love, nothing counts
summary: Without love, speaking in human or angelic tongues is mere noise, and prophecy, knowledge, mountain-moving faith, or giving all to the poor and handing over one's body counts for nothing.

title: What love looks like
summary: Love shows patience and kindness; it isn't envious, boastful, arrogant, rude, selfish or touchy, holds no grudges, delights in truth rather than wrong, and stays hopeful and steadfast through everything.

title: Love outlasts every gift
summary: Prophecy, tongues and knowledge are partial and will one day end, but love lasts forever; of faith, hope and love, which endure, love ranks highest.

title: Seek gifts that strengthen others
summary: Put love first and value gifts that serve others: prophecy addresses people to strengthen, urge on and console them, building up the whole church, not just oneself.

title: Speak so others can benefit
summary: Unintelligible speech helps no one, like an unclear trumpet call or an unknown language; believers keen on spiritual gifts should seek above all those that strengthen the church.

title: Help others understand and join in
summary: Pray and give thanks intelligibly so an uninitiated listener can join in and be built up; in church Paul prefers a few clear, teaching words to endless unintelligible ones.

title: Consider outsiders in your gatherings
summary: Unbelievers or newcomers entering a meeting full of tongues will think the church mad, but understandable prophecy can convict them, expose their hearts and lead them to worship God.

title: Let everything build others up
summary: Whatever each contributes when the church meets should build it up; speakers take turns and give way, others evaluate messages, and all learn, for God's way is peace, not chaos.

title: Watch who influences you
summary: Don't be naive: the wrong companions drag down good conduct; come to your senses and quit sinning, since some among you, shamefully, don't know God.

title: Set aside gifts for fellow believers
summary: For the collection for Jerusalem's believers, each person should put money aside weekly in keeping with their earnings, and the church should choose trusted people to deliver the gift.

title: Welcome Timothy and treat him well
summary: Paul asks the church to put Timothy at ease, as he too serves the Lord; nobody should look down on him, and they should send him off on good terms.

title: Let love drive everything
summary: In his closing charge, Paul tells the church to let love govern everything they do.

title: Honor those who serve faithfully
summary: Stephanas' household gave themselves to serving fellow believers; Paul urges the church to defer to such workers and to value men like Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus, who lifted everyone's spirits.

title: Greet one another warmly
summary: Churches in Asia, Aquila and Prisca, and the church meeting in their home send warm greetings; believers are to greet each other with a holy kiss.

title: Pass on the comfort you received
summary: God comforts believers in their troubles so they can comfort others in theirs, and sufferers and comforters share together in both the hardship and the relief.

title: Helping through prayer
summary: Paul trusts God to rescue him again and counts on the church to join in that rescue by praying for him, so that many will give thanks.

title: Sincere conduct toward everyone
summary: Paul can point to a clear conscience about how he has lived in the world, and especially among the Corinthians, with honest motives rather than worldly cunning.

title: Leaders serve joy, not control
summary: Paul held back from returning to spare the church, explaining that leaders do not control what people believe but work alongside them for their joy.

title: Correcting with tears and love
summary: Paul avoided a second painful visit and wrote a hard letter in great distress, intending to show his love for the church rather than to hurt them.

title: Forgive and comfort the offender
summary: After the church has disciplined someone enough, it should forgive and comfort him and affirm its love, so that he is not crushed by sorrow.

title: Forgiveness keeps Satan from gaining ground
summary: Paul joins the church in forgiving the offender, for their sake, so that Satan does not gain an advantage over them.

title: Honest, open ministry to everyone
summary: Paul gives up secret, deceptive methods and any bending of the message, and instead wins the trust of every conscience by stating the truth openly.

title: Proclaim Christ, not yourself
summary: Ministers do not promote themselves but proclaim Jesus as Lord, presenting themselves as servants of the people they serve for his sake.

title: Moved by Christ to persuade others
summary: Out of reverence for the Lord and the love of Christ, Paul works to persuade people, and those who live should live for Christ rather than themselves.

title: Ambassadors of reconciliation
summary: Believers no longer judge people by outward standards, and God, who no longer counts sins against people, makes them ambassadors urging others to be reconciled to him.

title: Give no cause for discredit
summary: Paul is careful never to place an obstacle in front of anyone, so that no one can discredit the ministry.

title: Commended by character under pressure
summary: Paul shows his ministry is genuine through endurance in hardship and through purity, patience, kindness, sincere love and truthful speech, whether he is honored or slandered.

title: Open your heart in return
summary: Paul has spoken frankly and kept his heart open toward the Corinthians, and he asks them as his children to open their hearts to him in the same way.

title: Avoid binding partnerships with unbelievers
summary: Believers should not enter close, binding partnerships with unbelievers because righteousness and wickedness, light and darkness share nothing, so they should stay separate from what defiles and pursue holiness.

title: Restoring warmth after strain
summary: Paul asks the church to make room for him, affirms he has wronged no one, and assures them he is not condemning them but holds them dear.

title: Comfort delivered through a friend
summary: God comforted the exhausted Paul through the arrival of Titus and the news that the Corinthians longed for him, mourned and showed concern for him.

title: Godly sorrow leads to repentance
summary: Paul does not regret his painful letter, since the sorrow it caused led the church to repent, and godly sorrow differs from worldly sorrow that brings only death.

title: Repentance shows in changed action
summary: Godly sorrow produced earnestness, eagerness to clear themselves and readiness to make things right, and Paul says he wrote so the church could see its own devotion.

title: Encouragement and confidence in others
summary: Paul is encouraged by how the church refreshed Titus and welcomed him, and he rejoices that he can speak well of them and trust them fully.

title: Generosity from deep poverty
summary: The Macedonian churches, though afflicted and very poor, begged for the chance to help fellow believers and gave eagerly beyond their means, first giving themselves to the Lord.

title: Excel in giving too
summary: Paul urges the Corinthians to finish their part in the collection and excel in giving, not as a command but as a way to prove their love.

title: Christ became poor for others
summary: Jesus, though rich, became poor for the sake of believers, setting the pattern for giving generously to those in need.

title: Give willingly from what you have
summary: The Corinthians are urged to complete the giving they began so eagerly, with the gift judged by what a person has, not by what they lack.

title: Fair sharing between churches
summary: Giving should not leave the givers burdened while others are relieved, but create fairness, with those who have extra meeting present needs and receiving help in return later.

title: Handle shared money above reproach
summary: Paul sends Titus and a brother praised by the churches to administer the collection, taking care to do right before both God and people so no one can criticize.

title: Honor trusted fellow workers
summary: Paul commends Titus and the other brothers as proven partners and messengers of the churches, and asks the Corinthians to show them love openly.

title: Be ready to give as promised
summary: Paul sends brothers ahead so the promised gift will be ready and given generously rather than reluctantly, since he has praised their eagerness to others.

title: Give freely and gladly
summary: Sowing generously brings a generous harvest, so each person should give what they have decided in their heart, gladly and not under pressure or with regret.

title: God supplies so you can give
summary: God provides enough that believers can abound in good works and be generous on every occasion, so their giving produces thanks to him.

title: Giving meets needs and stirs thanks
summary: Sharing with fellow believers supplies their needs and overflows in thanksgiving to God, and those who receive will pray for the givers with affection.

title: Appealing with gentleness, not force
summary: Paul appeals to the church in the gentleness of Christ, hoping he will not need to be bold with those who wrongly judge him when he arrives.

title: Authority is for building up
summary: Paul says the authority the Lord gave him is meant to strengthen the church, not to tear it down.

title: Do not compare or self-promote
summary: Paul refuses to compare himself with self-promoters or claim credit for the work of others, insisting that approval comes from the Lord, not from self-praise.

title: Do not tolerate a different gospel
summary: Paul fears the church will be led astray from devotion to Christ, and rebukes them for readily putting up with anyone who proclaims a different Jesus, spirit or gospel.

title: Serve without being a burden
summary: Paul preached without pay, relying on support from other churches so he would not burden the Corinthians, and says this shows his love for them.

title: Sharing the weakness of others
summary: Paul carries daily concern for all the churches, sharing the weakness of those who are weak and grieving intensely when someone is led into sin.

title: Accepting insults for Christ
summary: Learning that Christ's power is shown in weakness, Paul gladly accepts insults, hardships and persecution for Christ's sake.

title: Spend yourself for those you lead
summary: Paul refuses to burden the church because he seeks them, not their possessions, and gladly spends his own money and life for them as a parent does for children.

title: Leaders must not exploit others
summary: Paul answers the charge that he or the men he sent took advantage of the church, pointing to the shared integrity of his own conduct and that of Titus.

title: Fear of quarrels and rivalry
summary: Paul says all he writes is to build the church up, and he fears finding quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance and disorder when he arrives.

title: Warning those who have not repented
summary: Paul grieves over members who sinned and have not repented, cites the rule of two or three witnesses, and warns he will not spare them when he returns.

title: Pray for others to do right
summary: Paul prays that the church will do what is right, even if he appears to fail, and rejoices when they are strong while praying for their maturity.

title: Use authority to build up
summary: Paul writes in advance so he need not be severe when he arrives, since his authority from the Lord is meant to strengthen the church, not tear it down.

title: Aim for harmony and peace
summary: Believers are told to mend what is broken, encourage one another, think alike and live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with them.

title: Greet one another warmly
summary: Believers are told to greet one another with a sacred kiss, the affectionate greeting of that culture.

title: Reject a contrary gospel
summary: Paul pronounces a curse on anyone, even an angel, who preaches a gospel different from the one the Galatians received.

title: Praising God for a former persecutor
summary: Churches in Judea heard that their former persecutor was now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy, and they praised God because of him.

title: Paul consults leaders privately
summary: Paul went to Jerusalem and laid out his message privately before the recognized leaders, wanting to be sure his work would not prove futile.

title: Stand firm against false brothers
summary: Paul refused to yield even briefly to false brothers who slipped in to spy on the freedom believers have in Christ, protecting the truth of the gospel.

title: Leaders extend the hand of fellowship
summary: Paul is unimpressed by status since God shows no favoritism, and the Jerusalem leaders recognize his calling and offer him and Barnabas the hand of partnership.

title: Remember the poor
summary: The Jerusalem leaders ask Paul and Barnabas only to keep remembering the poor, which Paul was already eager to do.

title: Paul confronts Peter publicly
summary: Peter withdrew from eating with Gentile believers out of fear of the circumcision group, leading others astray, so Paul opposed him openly because this conduct contradicted the gospel.

title: One in Christ, no barriers
summary: All who belong to Christ are children of God by faith, and ethnic, social and gender divisions do not separate them because they are one in Christ.

title: Appeal to a warm friendship
summary: Paul appeals to the Galatians to share his outlook, recalling how warmly they welcomed him in his illness and affirming they had done him no wrong.

title: Truth-telling can cost goodwill
summary: Paul asks whether telling the truth has made him their enemy, warning that rivals court them with wrong motives in order to isolate them from him.

title: Pastoral anguish and tone
summary: Paul compares his struggle for the Galatians to labor pains until Christ takes shape in them, and wishes he could be present to speak differently because he is perplexed.

title: Serve in love, not in conflict
summary: Freedom is for serving one another in love, since loving a neighbor fulfills the whole law, while attacking and tearing at one another will end in mutual destruction.

title: Works of the flesh that divide
summary: Among the sinful works of the flesh are hatred, discord, jealousy, rage, rivalry, division, factions and envy, and those who live this way will not inherit the kingdom.

title: Fruit of the Spirit in relationships
summary: The Spirit produces love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control in believers, qualities no law opposes.

title: Keep in step, avoid conceit
summary: Since believers live by the Spirit they should follow his lead and not become arrogant, goad each other or resent each other.

title: Restore gently and share burdens
summary: Spiritual believers should gently restore someone caught in wrongdoing while guarding themselves against temptation, and should help one another with heavy burdens, which fulfills the law of Christ.

title: Assess yourself, do not compare
summary: Thinking too highly of oneself is self-deception, so each person should examine their own work, avoid comparing with others, and carry their own responsibility.

title: Share with those who teach you
summary: Those who are taught the word should share all good things with the one who instructs them.

title: Do good to everyone
summary: Believers should not tire of doing good, and as opportunity arises should do good to everyone, especially to fellow believers, expecting a harvest in due time.

title: Thankful prayer for loving believers
summary: Hearing of their faith and love for all the saints, Paul never stops thanking God for them and praying they grow in knowing Him.

title: Christ tore down the dividing wall
summary: Gentiles once excluded and far off have been brought near; Christ, our peace, tore down the dividing wall of hostility and made Jew and Gentile one body.

title: Fellow citizens in God's household
summary: Christ preached peace to those far and near, giving both access to the Father, so Gentiles are fellow citizens and members of God's household, built together.

title: Kneeling in prayer for others
summary: Paul kneels in prayer for the believers, asking that they be strengthened, rooted in love, and able together with all the saints to grasp Christ's vast love.

title: Keep the unity of the Spirit
summary: Walk worthy with humility, gentleness, and patience, bearing with one another in love and preserving unity through peace, because there is one body, Spirit, Lord, faith, and God.

title: Leaders equip everyone for ministry
summary: Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers to equip all the saints for ministry and build up the body until all reach unity and maturity.

title: Speak the truth in love
summary: Speaking the truth in love, we grow up into Christ, and the whole body builds itself up in love as each part does its work.

title: Speak truthfully to your neighbor
summary: Put away lying and speak truthfully to your neighbor, because believers are members of one another.

title: Don't let anger linger
summary: Be angry without sinning; don't let the sun set on your anger or give the devil a foothold.

title: Work so you can share
summary: The thief must stop stealing and do honest work with his hands so he has something to share with anyone in need.

title: Words that build others up
summary: Let no unwholesome talk come from your mouth, only words that build up others according to their need and give grace to hearers.

title: Forgive as God forgave you
summary: Get rid of bitterness, rage, anger, slander, and malice; instead be kind and tenderhearted, forgiving one another just as God forgave you in Christ.

title: Walk in love like Christ
summary: As God's beloved children, imitate Him and live a life of love, just as Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us.

title: No crude or foolish talk
summary: Obscenity, foolish talk, and crude joking don't fit God's people; let thanksgiving fill your speech instead.

title: Don't partner in darkness
summary: Don't be deceived by empty words or become partners with the disobedient; live as children of light and expose, rather than join, fruitless deeds of darkness.

title: Sing and speak to one another
summary: Speak to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, making music to the Lord and always giving thanks for everything.

title: Submit to one another
summary: Out of reverence for Christ, believers are to submit to one another, setting the tone for the household instructions that follow.

title: Wives, submit to your husbands
summary: Wives are to submit to their own husbands as to the Lord, as the church submits to Christ its head.

title: Husbands, love as Christ loved
summary: Husbands must love their wives as Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her, nourishing and cherishing them as their own bodies.

title: Love and respect in marriage
summary: Husband and wife become one flesh, a profound mystery speaking of Christ and the church; each husband must love his wife as himself, and the wife respect her husband.

title: Children, obey and honor parents
summary: Children are to obey their parents in the Lord and honor father and mother, the first commandment with a promise that life will go well.

title: Fathers, don't provoke your children
summary: Fathers must not provoke their children to anger but raise them in the Lord's discipline and instruction.

title: Work sincerely, as serving Christ
summary: Slaves should obey earthly masters with respect and sincerity, not just when watched, serving wholeheartedly as to the Lord, who rewards everyone's good work.

title: Masters, stop threatening
summary: Masters must treat their slaves the same way and give up threats, knowing they share a Master in heaven who shows no favoritism.

title: Pray for all the saints
summary: Keep praying persistently for all believers, and pray for Paul to proclaim the gospel boldly and fearlessly, even as an ambassador in chains.

title: Sending news to encourage hearts
summary: Paul sends Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful servant, to tell the church how he is doing and to encourage their hearts.

title: Partners held in the heart
summary: Paul joyfully thanks God and prays for the Philippians, his partners in the gospel, holding them in his heart and longing for them with Christ's affection.

title: Praying that love will abound
summary: Paul prays that their love will abound more and more in knowledge and insight, so they can discern what is best and live blamelessly.

title: Chains that emboldened others
summary: Paul's imprisonment advanced the gospel through the whole palace guard and emboldened most believers to speak the word without fear.

title: Rejoicing despite rival preachers
summary: Though some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, hoping to add to his distress, Paul refuses resentment and rejoices that Christ is preached either way.

title: Staying on for others' sake
summary: Though Paul longs to depart and be with Christ, he concludes it is more necessary for them that he remain, for their progress and joy in faith.

title: Stand together against opposition
summary: Live worthy of the gospel, standing firm in one spirit and contending side by side, unafraid of opponents, since suffering for Christ is part of your calling.

title: Value others above yourselves
summary: Be like-minded and united in love; do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but humbly consider others more important and look to their interests.

title: Have the mind of Christ
summary: Adopt Christ's attitude: though He existed in the form of God, He emptied Himself, took a servant's form, and humbled Himself to death on a cross.

title: No grumbling or arguing
summary: Do everything without complaining or arguing, so you are blameless children of God shining like lights in a crooked generation as you hold out the word of life.

title: Rejoice together, even in sacrifice
summary: Even if his life is poured out as an offering for their faith, Paul rejoices with them and asks them to rejoice with him.

title: Timothy's genuine care for others
summary: Paul commends Timothy as one who genuinely cares for the church's welfare, unlike others who seek their own interests, and who served beside him like a son.

title: Epaphroditus and mutual concern
summary: Epaphroditus ministered to Paul's needs and nearly died, yet worried about the church's worry for him; Paul sends him home so they can rejoice.

title: Honor those who risk for others
summary: Welcome Epaphroditus with great joy and honor people like him, who risk their lives for Christ's work and to serve others.

title: Beware of those distorting the gospel
summary: Watch out for those Paul calls dogs, evil workers, and mutilators of the flesh, who put confidence in physical circumcision rather than in Christ.

title: Follow good examples together
summary: Join in imitating Paul and those who live by his pattern, because many live as enemies of the cross, something Paul says with tears.

title: Help two coworkers reconcile
summary: Paul pleads with Euodia and Syntyche to agree in the Lord and asks a trusted partner to help these faithful coworkers settle their disagreement.

title: Let your gentleness be known
summary: Let your gentleness be evident to everyone, because the Lord is near.

title: Thanks for sharing in hardship
summary: Paul rejoices that the Philippians renewed their concern for him; though content in any circumstance, he commends them for sharing in his troubles.

title: Partners in giving and receiving
summary: The Philippians alone partnered with Paul in giving, repeatedly meeting his needs; he calls their gifts a sacrifice pleasing to God, who will supply their needs.

title: Known for loving all believers
summary: Paul thanks God because the Colossians' faith in Christ shows up as love for all of God's people.

title: Praying steadily for others
summary: From the day they heard about the Colossians, Paul and Timothy kept praying that they would know God's will and live in a way that pleases him.

title: Warning and teaching everyone
summary: Paul works hard proclaiming Christ, warning and teaching every person with wisdom so that each one can stand mature in Christ.

title: Hearts joined together in love
summary: Paul labors for believers he has never met, wanting them encouraged and joined together in love as they grow in understanding Christ.

title: Don't let others judge your observances
summary: Don't let anyone condemn you over food, drink or religious holidays; those practices were shadows, and the reality is Christ.

title: Get rid of anger and slander
summary: Put away anger, rage, malice, slander and foul language.

title: Stop lying to each other
summary: Don't lie to one another, because you have taken off the old self and put on a new self being renewed in God's image.

title: No ethnic or class divide
summary: In the new humanity there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or not, foreigner, slave or free; Christ is all and in all.

title: Put on compassion, forgiveness, love
summary: As God's chosen people, put on compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience; bear with each other, forgive as the Lord forgave you, and above all put on love.

title: Let Christ's peace rule
summary: Let the peace of Christ settle things in your hearts, since you were called to peace as members of one body, and be thankful.

title: Teach and admonish one another
summary: Let Christ's word fill you as you teach and correct one another with wisdom and sing to God with thankful hearts.

title: Wives and husbands
summary: Wives, submit to your husbands as fits life in the Lord; husbands, love your wives and never treat them harshly.

title: Children and fathers
summary: Children, obey your parents, which pleases the Lord; fathers, don't provoke your children, or they will lose heart.

title: Work as serving the Lord
summary: Slaves should obey their masters sincerely, not just when watched, working wholeheartedly for the Lord, who repays wrongdoing without favoritism.

title: Masters, be just and fair
summary: Masters must give their slaves what is right and fair, knowing they also have a Master in heaven.

title: Pray for open doors
summary: Keep praying with thanks, and pray that God opens a door for the message and that Paul can proclaim Christ clearly.

title: Wise and gracious with outsiders
summary: Live wisely toward outsiders and use every opportunity; let your speech always be gracious and thoughtful, so you know how to answer each person.

title: Sent to encourage hearts
summary: Paul sends Tychicus to bring news and encourage the church, along with Onesimus, whom he now calls a faithful, beloved brother.

title: Welcome Mark if he comes
summary: Paul tells the church to welcome Mark, Barnabas's cousin, the same Mark that Paul once refused to take along (Acts 15:37-39).

title: Epaphras wrestles in prayer
summary: Epaphras keeps laboring in prayer for the Colossians and nearby churches, asking that they stand mature and fully assured in God's will.

title: Thankful prayer for fellow believers
summary: Paul's team thanks God for the Thessalonians in constant prayer, recalling how their faith produced work, their love put in effort, and their hope endured.

title: Joyful faith that spread outward
summary: Despite heavy suffering, the Thessalonians embraced the gospel with Spirit-given joy, became a model for believers throughout Macedonia and Achaia, and the Lord's message spread from them everywhere.

title: Bold witness after mistreatment
summary: After being insulted and mistreated in Philippi, Paul and his companions still spoke the gospel boldly in Thessalonica, relying on God in the face of fierce opposition.

title: No flattery, greed, or self-promotion
summary: Paul and his coworkers came without deceit, flattery, hidden greed, or hunger for praise, aiming to please God rather than people and not pressing their rights as apostles.

title: Gentle care that shares life
summary: Paul's team was as tender as a mother caring for her little ones, loving the believers so much they gladly shared their very lives along with the gospel.

title: Working so as not to burden
summary: Paul's team worked hard night and day to support themselves rather than burden anyone while preaching, and conducted themselves with integrity among the believers.

title: Fatherly encouragement for each one
summary: Like a father with his children, Paul's team dealt with each believer personally, encouraging, comforting, and urging them to live lives worthy of the God who calls them.

title: Longing to see them again
summary: Separated from the believers, Paul ached to see them face to face and kept trying to come back, calling them his hope, joy, and glory at the Lord's return.

title: Sending Timothy to strengthen them
summary: Unable to bear not knowing how they fared under persecution, Paul stayed alone in Athens and sent Timothy to strengthen and encourage their faith so trials wouldn't unsettle them.

title: Comforted by their faith and love
summary: Timothy's report of their faith, love, and longing to see Paul encouraged him amid his own hardships, and he prays earnestly night and day to visit and strengthen them.

title: Love that overflows to everyone
summary: Paul prays the Lord will make their love grow and overflow toward each other and toward all people, as his does for them, establishing their hearts in holiness.

title: Never wrong a brother sexually
summary: Part of God's call to sexual purity and self-control: no one may wrong or take advantage of a fellow believer this way, for the Lord punishes such wrongs.

title: Keep loving; live quietly and work
summary: God has taught you to love each other; keep growing in it, live quietly, mind your own affairs and work, winning outsiders' respect and depending on no one.

title: Comfort each other with hope
summary: Because believers who have died will rise and all will be with the Lord together, comfort and encourage one another with this hope.

title: Keep strengthening one another
summary: In light of the hope of salvation through Christ, keep encouraging each other and strengthening one another's faith, as you are already doing.

title: Respect leaders; keep the peace
summary: Appreciate the leaders who work hard among you, guiding and instructing you; honor them warmly for their work, and keep peace among yourselves.

title: Match care to each need
summary: Warn those who are idle or disorderly, cheer up the discouraged, support the weak, and be patient with everyone.

title: Never pay back wrong with wrong
summary: Make sure nobody pays back a wrong with another wrong; always seek the good of fellow believers and of everyone else.

title: Pray for us; greet everyone warmly
summary: Paul asks the believers to pray for him and his coworkers, and to greet all their brothers and sisters with a kiss of holy affection.

title: Growing love amid persecution
summary: Paul thanks God that the believers' faith is flourishing and their love for each other keeps increasing, and he boasts of their steadfast endurance under persecution.

title: Praying for one another's growth
summary: Paul constantly prays that God will make the believers worthy of his calling and fulfill their good intentions and acts of faith, so Jesus is honored in them.

title: Pray for the message to spread
summary: Pray for Paul's team that the Lord's message spreads quickly and is honored as it was among you, and that they're rescued from wicked people, since not all have faith.

title: Withdraw from those who refuse work
summary: Keep away from any believer living idly against Paul's teaching; follow his example of working hard so as not to burden anyone—whoever refuses to work should not eat.

title: Busybodies should work quietly
summary: Some were idle meddlers doing nothing useful; Paul commands them to settle down, work, and earn their own living, and urges everyone else not to tire of doing good.

title: Correct as family, not foe
summary: If someone ignores the apostle's instructions, identify him and keep your distance so he feels ashamed, yet treat him as a brother to correct, not as a foe.

title: Stop false teaching at the source
summary: Timothy should stay in Ephesus and direct certain people to stop teaching false doctrine and chasing myths that breed speculation instead of faith.

title: The goal is love
summary: The aim of all this instruction is love flowing from a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith.

title: Discipline meant to teach
summary: Paul says Hymenaeus and Alexander rejected their conscience and wrecked their faith, so he handed them over to Satan to learn not to blaspheme.

title: Pray for everyone, including rulers
summary: Pray and give thanks for all people, including kings and officials, so we can live quiet, godly lives; God wants everyone to be saved.

title: Pray without anger or arguing
summary: Paul wants men everywhere to pray with holy hands raised, without anger or quarreling.

title: Leaders: hospitable, gentle, not quarrelsome
summary: An overseer must be hospitable and able to teach, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and not a lover of money.

title: Lead your own home well
summary: An overseer must manage his household well and keep his children in order with dignity; if he can't manage his home, how can he care for God's church?

title: Respected by outsiders
summary: A church leader must have a good reputation with outsiders, so he doesn't fall into disgrace and the devil's trap.

title: Deacons: honest speech, ordered homes
summary: Deacons must be serious and not two-faced in speech; the women must not be slanderers; and each must manage children and household well.

title: Be an example to believers
summary: Don't let anyone look down on your youth; set an example for believers in speech, conduct, love, faith and purity.

title: Treat the church like family
summary: Don't rebuke an older man harshly but appeal to him as a father; treat younger men as brothers, older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, in all purity.

title: Families care for their widows
summary: Honor widows who are truly alone; if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first practice godliness by caring for their own family and repaying their parents.

title: Provide for your own household
summary: Anyone who won't provide for relatives, especially their own household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

title: Known for hospitality and service
summary: A widow put on the church's support list should be known for good works: raising children, welcoming strangers, washing believers' feet and helping those in trouble.

title: Don't drift into gossip
summary: Paul warns that idle house-to-house visiting can turn into gossip and meddling, and wants younger widows to marry and manage homes so opponents have no grounds for slander.

title: Support the widows in your family
summary: A believing woman with widowed relatives should support them herself, so the church isn't burdened and can care for widows who have no one.

title: Honor and pay faithful elders
summary: Elders who lead well deserve double honor, especially those who preach and teach, because workers deserve their wages.

title: Accusations against leaders need witnesses
summary: Don't accept a charge against an elder without two or three witnesses; elders who keep on sinning should be rebuked publicly as a warning to others.

title: No partiality, no favorites
summary: Paul solemnly charges Timothy to apply these instructions without prejudice and to do nothing out of favoritism.

title: Honor masters, believing or not
summary: Slaves should treat their masters with full respect so God's name isn't slandered; those with believing masters shouldn't disrespect them as brothers but serve them even better.

title: Controversy breeds envy and strife
summary: Someone obsessed with controversies and arguments over words produces envy, strife, slander, suspicion and constant friction, and treats godliness as a way to profit.

title: Wealthy? Be generous and share
summary: Tell the wealthy not to be proud or trust riches, but to do good, be rich in good works, and be generous and ready to share.

title: Praying and longing for a friend
summary: Paul prays for Timothy night and day, remembers his tears, and longs to see him again.

title: Faith passed down at home
summary: Timothy's sincere faith first lived in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice, and Paul is sure it lives in him too.

title: Don't be ashamed of the imprisoned
summary: Don't be ashamed of testifying about the Lord or of Paul his prisoner; share in suffering for the gospel by God's power.

title: Onesiphorus wasn't ashamed of chains
summary: When others in Asia deserted Paul, Onesiphorus searched Rome until he found him, often refreshed him, and wasn't ashamed of his chains.

title: Pass it on to faithful people
summary: Entrust what you learned from Paul to reliable people who will be able to teach others too.

title: Don't quarrel about words
summary: Remind believers and warn them before God not to fight over words, which helps no one and ruins those listening.

title: Avoid talk that spreads like infection
summary: Avoid godless chatter, which leads to more ungodliness and spreads like gangrene, as with two men whose false teaching unsettles others' faith.

title: Pursue peace with sincere believers
summary: Flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

title: Correct opponents gently
summary: Refuse foolish debates that breed fights; the Lord's servant must be kind to everyone, patient, and gentle in correcting opponents, hoping God grants them repentance.

title: Avoid the cruel and self-centered
summary: In the last days people will be selfish, abusive, unloving, unforgiving, slanderous and brutal while keeping a show of godliness; avoid such people.

title: Godly living draws persecution
summary: Timothy saw Paul's patience, love and endurance through persecutions; everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ will be persecuted.

title: Correct and encourage patiently
summary: Preach the word at every opportunity; correct, rebuke and encourage with great patience and careful teaching.

title: Do the work of an evangelist
summary: Stay clear-headed, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill your ministry.

title: Mark is useful to me now
summary: Demas deserted Paul for love of this world, but Paul asks for Mark, whom he once refused to take along, because Mark is now useful to him.

title: Leave repayment to the Lord
summary: Alexander the coppersmith did Paul great harm; Paul leaves repayment to the Lord but warns Timothy to watch out for him.

title: Abandoned, but not holding grudges
summary: When everyone abandoned Paul at his first defense, he asked that it not be held against them; the Lord stood with him so the Gentiles could hear.

title: Elders with faithful families
summary: Titus is to appoint elders in every town who are blameless, husbands of one wife, with believing children who aren't wild or rebellious.

title: Leaders not hot-tempered
summary: An overseer must not be arrogant, quick-tempered, a drunkard, violent or greedy, but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled and disciplined.

title: Encourage and refute
summary: An elder must hold to the trustworthy message so he can encourage others with sound teaching and correct those who oppose it.

title: Stop deceivers who upset households
summary: Many deceivers are upsetting whole families for profit; they must be silenced, and Titus should rebuke them sharply so they become sound in the faith.

title: Older believers train younger ones
summary: Older men should be sober and sound in faith and love; older women, not slanderers, should teach younger women to love their husbands and children, so God's word isn't maligned.

title: Give opponents nothing to criticize
summary: Urge younger men to self-control; Titus must model good works and sound, dignified speech so opponents are embarrassed, finding nothing to criticize.

title: Honest, agreeable work
summary: Slaves should please their masters, not argue back or steal, but prove fully trustworthy, so their lives make the teaching about God attractive.

title: Encourage and correct with authority
summary: Teach these things, encouraging and rebuking with full authority, and don't let anyone disregard you.

title: Gentle and courteous to everyone
summary: Remind believers to submit to rulers, be ready for every good work, speak evil of no one, avoid fighting, and show gentleness and courtesy to all people.

title: Remember who we used to be
summary: Be gentle with everyone, because we too once lived in malice and envy, hated and hating, until God's kindness appeared and saved us by mercy.

title: Devoted to good works
summary: Stress these truths so believers will be careful to devote themselves to good works, which are excellent and beneficial for people.

title: Avoid foolish controversies
summary: Avoid foolish debates, genealogies, arguments and fights about the law, because they are useless and worthless.

title: Warn a divisive person twice
summary: After warning a divisive person once and then a second time, have nothing more to do with him; such a person is twisted and self-condemned.

title: Meet urgent needs
summary: Help Zenas and Apollos on their way with everything they need, and teach our people to devote themselves to good works that meet urgent needs.

title: Love that refreshes hearts
summary: Paul thanks God for Philemon's faith and love for all the saints, whose hearts Philemon has refreshed, bringing Paul great joy and comfort.

title: Appeal in love, don't command
summary: Though Paul could order Philemon to do what is right, he chooses to appeal to him on the basis of love.

title: Sending Onesimus back
summary: Paul sends back Onesimus, who became his spiritual son in prison, and won't keep him without Philemon's consent so any kindness is freely given.

title: Welcome him back as a brother
summary: Paul asks Philemon to take Onesimus back no longer merely as a slave but as a dear brother, welcoming him as he would welcome Paul.

title: Charge his debt to me
summary: If Onesimus wronged Philemon or owes anything, Paul will repay it himself, and he trusts Philemon to do even more than he asks.

title: Exhort one another every day
summary: Make sure no one among you develops an unbelieving heart that turns from God; exhort one another daily so that sin's deceitfulness hardens no one.

title: Keep on serving the saints
summary: God will not forget the love you have shown by serving fellow believers; keep showing that same diligence to the very end.

title: Spur one another on
summary: Think about how to stir one another up to love and good deeds; don't give up meeting together, but keep encouraging each other as the Day approaches.

title: Standing with persecuted believers
summary: In their early days these believers endured public insult and persecution, stood alongside others so treated, sympathized with prisoners, and joyfully accepted the seizure of their property.

title: Defying Pharaoh by faith
summary: Moses' parents hid him, unafraid of the king's edict; Moses chose mistreatment with God's people over sin's pleasures and left Egypt unafraid of the king's anger.

title: Enduring mockery, chains, and death
summary: By faith others were tortured yet refused release, and endured mocking, flogging, chains, stoning, and destitution—people of whom the world was not worthy.

title: Consider Jesus under hostility
summary: When opposition wears you down, consider Jesus, who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you do not grow weary and lose heart.

title: Make straight paths for the lame
summary: Strengthen your weak hands and knees and make level paths, so that what is lame isn't disabled but healed.

title: Pursue peace, uproot bitterness
summary: Strive for peace with everyone and for holiness; watch that no one falls short of God's grace and that no bitter root springs up to trouble and defile many.

title: Brotherly love and hospitality
summary: Keep loving one another as brothers, and don't neglect hospitality to strangers, since some have entertained angels without knowing it.

title: Remember prisoners and the mistreated
summary: Remember those in prison as though you were in chains with them, and those who are mistreated as though you were suffering alongside them.

title: Honor marriage
summary: Everyone should hold marriage in honor and keep the marriage bed undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.

title: Remember and imitate your leaders
summary: Remember the leaders who taught you God's word; consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.

title: Bear the disgrace Jesus bore
summary: Go out to Jesus outside the camp and share the disgrace He bore, since believers have no permanent city here but look for the one to come.

title: Do good and share
summary: Don't neglect doing good and sharing what you have with others, because God is pleased with such sacrifices.

title: Follow and support your leaders
summary: Obey and submit to your leaders, who keep watch over your souls and must give an account; let them lead with joy rather than grief.

title: Pray for those who minister
summary: The writer, who has a clear conscience and wants to live honorably, asks for the believers' prayers, especially that he may soon be restored to them.

title: Status reversed for rich and poor
summary: The lowly believer should take pride in being lifted up, and the rich in being brought low, since wealth fades like a wildflower.

title: Quick to listen, slow to anger
summary: Be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry, because human anger does not produce the righteousness God desires.

title: Bridle your tongue
summary: Anyone who considers himself religious but does not rein in his tongue deceives himself, and his religion is worthless.

title: Care for orphans and widows
summary: Religion that God accepts means looking after orphans and widows in their distress and keeping yourself unpolluted by the world.

title: Don't play favorites
summary: Don't show favoritism: fawning over a well-dressed visitor while telling a poor one to stand or sit at your feet makes you judges with evil thoughts.

title: Don't dishonor the poor
summary: God chose the poor to be rich in faith and heirs of His kingdom, yet you dishonor them, though it's the rich who oppress you and blaspheme His name.

title: Favoritism breaks the royal law
summary: Loving your neighbor as yourself fulfills the royal law, but favoritism is sin, and breaking the law at one point makes you guilty of all of it.

title: Mercy triumphs over judgment
summary: Speak and act as people who will be judged by the law of freedom, for judgment without mercy awaits the merciless, but mercy triumphs over judgment.

title: Meet needs, don't just wish well
summary: Telling a brother or sister who lacks clothes and food to stay warm and well fed, without providing for them, is useless; faith without action is dead.

title: Teachers and the tongue
summary: Not many should become teachers, since teachers will be judged more strictly; we all stumble, and anyone who never errs in speech can control his whole body.

title: A small tongue, a great fire
summary: Small like a horse's bit or a ship's rudder, the tongue has outsized power; like a spark it can set a forest ablaze and corrupt a whole life.

title: Don't bless God and curse people
summary: No one can tame the tongue, yet with it we praise God and curse people made in His likeness; blessing and cursing from one mouth should not be.

title: Jealousy and ambition breed disorder
summary: Show wisdom through good conduct done in humility; bitter jealousy and selfish ambition are earthly, even demonic, and produce disorder and every evil practice.

title: Peace-loving wisdom from above
summary: Wisdom from above is pure, peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, merciful, impartial, and sincere, and peacemakers who sow in peace reap a harvest of righteousness.

title: Where quarrels come from
summary: Fights and quarrels among you come from selfish desires at war within you; you covet and fight instead of asking God, or you ask with wrong motives.

title: Repent and humble yourselves
summary: Addressing the quarrelers: friendship with the world is hostility toward God, so submit to Him, resist the devil, repent, and humble yourselves before the Lord.

title: Don't slander or judge
summary: Don't speak against one another; whoever slanders or judges a brother sets himself above the law, yet there is only one Lawgiver and Judge—who are you to judge?

title: Warning to rich who exploit workers
summary: A warning: the rich who hoard wealth, withhold workers' wages, live in luxury, and condemn and kill the righteous will face misery, for the harvesters' cries reach the Lord.

title: Be patient under oppression
summary: Wronged by the rich, believers should be patient until the Lord comes, like a farmer waiting for rain, and strengthen their hearts because His coming is near.

title: Don't grumble against each other
summary: Don't complain about one another, brothers, or you will be judged, for the Judge is standing at the door.

title: Endure like the prophets
summary: Take the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name as models of patience in affliction, and remember Job's perseverance and the Lord's compassion and mercy.

title: Let your yes mean yes
summary: Don't swear oaths by heaven, earth, or anything else; simply let your yes be yes and your no be no, so you won't fall under judgment.

title: Elders pray over the sick
summary: The sick should call the church's elders to pray over them and anoint them in the Lord's name; the prayer of faith will restore them.

title: Confess and pray for each other
summary: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another so that you may be healed; a righteous person's prayer is powerful and effective.

title: Bring back a wandering believer
summary: When a believer wanders from the truth and someone brings him back, know that turning a sinner from his error saves his soul from death and covers many sins.

title: Love one another deeply
summary: Since you've purified yourselves by obeying the truth and been born again through God's enduring word, love one another deeply and sincerely, from a pure heart.

title: Put away malice and slander
summary: Rid yourselves of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and every kind of slander.

title: Called to proclaim God's virtues
summary: Believers are God's chosen people and royal priesthood, called to proclaim the virtues of the One who called them out of darkness into His light.

title: Live honorably among unbelievers
summary: As foreigners and exiles, abstain from fleshly desires and live honorably among unbelievers, so that though they slander you, they see your good deeds and glorify God.

title: Submit to governing authorities
summary: For the Lord's sake submit to every human institution—the king and the governors he sends—since God wants your good conduct to silence foolish people's ignorance.

title: Honor everyone, love the brotherhood
summary: Live as free people but as God's servants, never using freedom to cover evil; honor everyone, love your fellow believers, fear God, and honor the king.

title: Respect even unreasonable masters
summary: Servants should submit respectfully to masters, both kind and unreasonable; enduring unjust suffering because you are mindful of God is commendable, unlike being punished for wrongdoing.

title: Follow Christ's non-retaliation
summary: Christ left an example to follow: when insulted He did not retaliate, when suffering He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to God, who judges justly.

title: Winning an unbelieving husband
summary: Wives should submit to their husbands so that any who reject the word may be won over without words by seeing their wives' pure, reverent conduct.

title: A gentle and quiet spirit
summary: Wives should prize a gentle, quiet spirit over outward adornment, like the holy women who hoped in God and submitted to their husbands, doing right without fear.

title: Husbands, honor your wives
summary: Husbands should treat their wives considerately, as a delicate vessel, honoring them as fellow heirs of the gift of life, so their prayers aren't hindered.

title: Like-minded, tender, and humble
summary: All of you should be like-minded and sympathetic, love one another as brothers, and be tenderhearted and humble.

title: Repay insult with blessing
summary: Don't repay evil for evil or insult for insult, but bless instead; whoever wants a good life must guard his tongue, turn from evil, and pursue peace.

title: Blessed when suffering for right
summary: Those eager to do good are blessed even when they suffer for doing right, so they should not fear what others fear or be shaken.

title: Answer with gentleness and respect
summary: Honor Christ as Lord and always be ready to explain your hope to anyone who asks, gently and respectfully, keeping a clear conscience so slanderers are put to shame.

title: When old companions heap abuse
summary: Former companions find it strange that believers no longer join their reckless living and heap abuse on them, but they will answer to the Judge of all.

title: Love covers many sins
summary: Above all, keep loving one another deeply, because love covers a great many sins.

title: Hospitality without grumbling
summary: Open your homes to one another without complaining.

title: Use your gifts to serve
summary: As stewards of God's varied grace, use whatever gift you have received to serve one another, speaking and serving in God's strength so He is glorified.

title: Blessed when insulted for Christ
summary: Don't be surprised by fiery trials as if something strange were happening; rejoice to share Christ's sufferings, and know you are blessed when insulted for His name.

title: Suffer as a Christian, not meddler
summary: Don't suffer as a murderer, thief, wrongdoer, or meddler; but if you suffer for being a Christian, don't be ashamed—glorify God for bearing that name.

title: Keep doing good while suffering
summary: Those who suffer according to God's will should entrust themselves to their faithful Creator and keep on doing good.

title: Shepherd the flock willingly
summary: Elders should shepherd God's flock willingly and eagerly, not for gain, not domineering over those in their charge, but being examples to the flock.

title: Clothe yourselves with humility
summary: Younger people should submit to the elders, and everyone should put on humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

title: Greet one another warmly
summary: Greet one another with a kiss of love; peace to all who are in Christ.

title: Add brotherly kindness and love
summary: Make every effort to build on your faith a chain of qualities that culminates in brotherly kindness and, finally, love.

title: Guard against false teachers' error
summary: Since you know that unstable people twist the Scriptures, stay on guard so that the error of lawless people does not carry you away.

title: Living in the light together
summary: When believers live in the light as God Himself is in the light, they share true fellowship with one another, and Jesus' blood cleanses them from every sin.

title: Hating a brother means darkness
summary: Claiming to be in the light while hating a fellow believer means you are still in darkness, blinded and lost; whoever loves a brother stays in the light.

title: Hold to what you first heard
summary: Since some are trying to mislead you, keep the message you heard from the start living in you and remain in Christ, as the anointing you received teaches you.

title: Love one another, unlike Cain
summary: Not loving a brother marks someone as not belonging to God; love one another, unlike Cain, who murdered his brother because his actions were evil and his brother's were good.

title: Expect hostility from the world
summary: Right after Cain's example, John tells believers not to be surprised when the world hates them.

title: Hating a brother is murder
summary: Love for fellow believers shows we have moved from death into life; the one who doesn't love stays in death, and whoever hates a brother is a murderer.

title: Love in deeds, not just words
summary: Jesus gave His life for us, so we should give our lives for each other, meeting a brother's material needs and loving through real deeds rather than mere words.

title: Believe and love one another
summary: God's command is twofold: trust in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and love one another as He instructed.

title: Test teachers before trusting them
summary: With many false prophets around, don't accept every spiritual claim; test it by whether it confesses Jesus Christ came in the flesh, knowing the world listens to its own.

title: God loved us; love each other
summary: Love one another, because love comes from God and the unloving don't know Him; since God sent His Son for our sins, we ought to love each other too.

title: Loving God means loving your brother
summary: Our love answers God's love; claiming to love God while hating a brother is a lie, since you can't love the unseen God without loving the brother you see.

title: Love all of God's children
summary: Everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is God's child, and loving the Father includes loving His children; we know we love them when we love God and obey Him.

title: Pray for a sinning brother
summary: Pray for a fellow believer whose sin does not lead to death, and God will give him life; John does not urge such prayer for sin that leads to death.

title: The original command: love one another
summary: John urges his readers to keep the command they have had from the start, to love one another, explaining that love means living by God's commands.

title: Don't host teachers who distort Christ
summary: Watch out for deceivers who deny Jesus Christ came in the flesh; don't give hospitality or a welcome to anyone who abandons Christ's teaching, or you join in his wrongdoing.

title: Praying for a friend's wellbeing
summary: John prays for his friend Gaius's health and wellbeing and rejoices at reports from visiting believers that Gaius is faithfully living by the truth.

title: Support traveling gospel workers
summary: Gaius faithfully helps visiting believers, even strangers; send such workers on in a God-honoring way, since they take nothing from pagans; supporting them makes us partners in their work.

title: A leader who craves first place
summary: A warning: status-seeking Diotrephes rejects John's instruction, spreads vicious gossip about him, refuses hospitality to visiting believers, and expels those who want to help; John plans to confront him.

title: Imitate good examples like Demetrius
summary: Don't copy what is evil but what is good, since doing good shows you belong to God; Demetrius is well spoken of by everyone, and John vouches for him too.

title: Greet each friend by name
summary: John hopes to visit soon and talk in person, passes along greetings from friends with him, and asks Gaius to greet each friend there individually.

title: Defend the faith against infiltrators
summary: Jude urges believers to fight for the faith God handed to His people, because godless men have secretly slipped in, using grace as an excuse for immorality and denying Christ.

title: Even Michael didn't hurl insults
summary: Even the archangel Michael, disputing with the devil, didn't bring an insulting accusation against him but left the rebuke to the Lord.

title: Stay steady amid divisive mockers
summary: Remember the apostles warned that mockers driven by godless desires would come and create divisions; strengthen yourselves in the faith, pray in the Spirit, and stay in God's love.

title: Show mercy to those who waver
summary: Be merciful to those who doubt, rescue others as if pulling them from a fire, and show still others mercy mixed with caution, hating even what their sin has stained.

title: Testing false apostles, enduring hardship
summary: Jesus commends the Ephesian church for not putting up with evildoers, testing would-be apostles and finding them frauds, and enduring hardship for His name without giving up.

title: Return to the love you had
summary: A warning: Jesus faults Ephesus for leaving the love they had at first, calling them to recall what they lost, repent, and return to their earlier deeds.

title: Rejecting the Nicolaitans' practices
summary: Jesus credits Ephesus for hating the practices of the Nicolaitans, practices He hates as well.

title: Don't fear suffering; stay faithful
summary: Jesus tells the poor, slandered church in Smyrna not to fear coming imprisonment and suffering but to stay faithful even if it means death, promising them the reward of life.

title: Not denying Christ under threat
summary: Jesus commends the church in hostile Pergamum for clinging to His name and not renouncing their faith, even when Antipas, who stayed true to Him, was killed among them.

title: Tolerating teaching that leads astray
summary: A warning: Jesus rebukes Pergamum for harboring some who hold Balaam-like and Nicolaitan teaching that lures believers into idolatry and immorality; repent, He says, or He will fight them.

title: Growing in love and service
summary: Jesus commends the church in Thyatira for its love, faith, service and perseverance, noting that what they are doing now exceeds what they did at first.

title: Tolerating a false prophetess
summary: A warning: Jesus rebukes Thyatira for tolerating the woman He calls Jezebel, a self-proclaimed prophetess who leads His servants into immorality and idolatry and refuses to repent.

title: Staying faithful with little strength
summary: Jesus commends the church in Philadelphia, weak as it is, for patient endurance and not denying Him, promising to make their opponents bow before them and know He loves them.

title: Faithful testimony even facing death
summary: A heavenly voice celebrates believers who defeated the accuser by the Lamb's blood and their testimony, not clinging to life even in the face of death.

title: Patient endurance under hostile power
summary: With the beast waging war on God's people, those destined for captivity or the sword will meet it, and this calls believers to patient endurance and faithfulness.

title: Kindness and faithfulness earn trust
summary: Never let steadfast love and faithfulness slip away; keep them close, and you will earn favor and a good reputation with God and people.

title: Help now, not tomorrow
summary: When it is in your power to do good for someone who needs it, do it; don't tell a neighbor to come back tomorrow when you can help today.

title: Don't scheme or pick fights
summary: Don't plot harm against a neighbor who lives trustingly beside you, and don't start a fight with someone who has done you no wrong.

title: God favors the humble
summary: God scorns those who scorn others but gives grace to the humble.

title: Things God hates, including discord
summary: Among the seven things the Lord hates are arrogance, lying, false testimony, and stirring up conflict among brothers.

title: Who welcomes correction
summary: Correcting a scoffer earns you insults and hatred, but correct a wise person and he will love you and grow wiser still.

title: Love covers offenses
summary: Hatred stirs up conflict, but love covers over every wrong.

title: Fewer words, fewer sins
summary: Where words pile up, sin is hard to avoid; whoever holds back his words is wise.

title: Don't belittle your neighbor
summary: Belittling a neighbor shows a lack of sense; a person of understanding keeps quiet.

title: Keep a confidence
summary: A gossip gives away secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.

title: Safety in many advisers
summary: Without guidance a people falls, but there is safety in an abundance of counselors.

title: The generous are refreshed
summary: One person gives freely and gains even more, while another holds back and ends up in need; whoever refreshes others will be refreshed.

title: Listen to advice
summary: A fool is sure his own way is right, but a wise person listens to advice.

title: Overlook an insult
summary: A fool shows his irritation right away, but a sensible person ignores an insult.

title: Words that wound or heal
summary: Careless words cut like a sword, but the words of the wise bring healing.

title: Joy for those who promote peace
summary: Deceit fills the hearts of those who plot evil, but people who work for peace have joy.

title: A kind word lifts anxiety
summary: Anxiety weighs a person down, but a good word cheers him up.

title: Pride breeds quarrels
summary: Arrogance produces nothing but strife, but wisdom belongs to those who take advice.

title: You become like your companions
summary: Walk with the wise and you will grow wise, but the companion of fools will suffer for it.

title: Don't look down on your neighbor
summary: Despising your neighbor is sin, but blessed is the person who is generous to the poor.

title: Slow to anger shows understanding
summary: Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding, but a quick temper puts folly on display.

title: Kindness to the needy honors God
summary: Oppressing the poor insults their Maker, but kindness to the needy honors him.

title: A gentle answer calms anger
summary: Answering gently defuses someone's anger, while a harsh reply only inflames it.

title: Gentle words give life
summary: Gentle words are a source of life, but twisted, cruel words crush a person's spirit.

title: Love matters more than the menu
summary: A plain meal shared with love is better than a lavish feast served with hatred.
