title: Patience calms a dispute
summary: A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but someone slow to anger settles quarrels.

title: Plans need many advisers
summary: Plans fail without counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.

title: Think before you answer
summary: The righteous weigh their answers carefully, while the wicked blurt out whatever is evil.

title: Welcome correction
summary: Whoever listens to life-giving correction will live among the wise; ignoring discipline means despising yourself.

title: Even enemies at peace
summary: When someone's ways please the Lord, he can make even that person's enemies live at peace with him.

title: Pride comes before a fall
summary: Pride leads to destruction and arrogance to a fall; better to be humble among the lowly than share plunder with the proud.

title: Gracious words are healing
summary: Kind, gracious words are like honey: sweet to the soul and healing to the body.

title: Gossip separates close friends
summary: A troublemaker spreads conflict, and a gossip splits up close friends.

title: Self-control beats strength
summary: Being slow to anger is better than being a mighty warrior, and ruling your temper is greater than capturing a city.

title: Peace at home over plenty
summary: A dry crust eaten in peace is better than a house full of feasting and fighting.

title: Cover an offense
summary: Whoever covers over a wrong builds love, but whoever keeps bringing it up separates close friends.

title: Stop a quarrel early
summary: Starting a quarrel is like opening a floodgate, so drop the matter before the dispute breaks out.

title: A friend loves at all times
summary: A true friend's love doesn't quit, and a brother is born to stand with you in hard times.

title: Restraint in words
summary: A person of knowledge uses words sparingly and keeps a cool head; even a fool seems wise when he stays quiet.

title: Isolation feeds selfishness
summary: Someone who isolates himself chases his own desires and rejects all sound judgment.

title: Understand before you opine
summary: A fool doesn't care about understanding; he only wants to air his own opinions.

title: Hear it out first
summary: Answering before you've heard the whole matter is foolish and shameful.

title: Hear both sides
summary: The first person to tell his side seems right, until the other person comes and questions him.

title: Winning back an offended brother
summary: A brother who has been wronged is harder to win back than a fortified city, and quarrels shut people out like barred gates.

title: The tongue's power
summary: The tongue holds the power of life and death, and those who love to talk will live with the results.

title: A friend closer than a brother
summary: Someone with many companions can still come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.

title: Overlook an offense
summary: Good sense makes a person slow to anger, and it is to his glory to let an offense go.

title: Lending to the Lord
summary: Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the Lord, and the Lord will repay him.

title: Stay out of strife
summary: It is honorable to steer clear of strife, but any fool is quick to quarrel.

title: Draw out what's in the heart
summary: A person's real purposes lie deep like water, but someone with understanding knows how to draw them out.

title: Avoid the gossip
summary: Someone who goes around gossiping gives away secrets, so don't spend time with a person who can't stop talking.

title: Leave payback to the Lord
summary: Don't vow to get even for a wrong; wait for the Lord, and he will deliver you.

title: Don't ignore the poor
summary: Whoever closes his ears to the cry of the poor will himself cry out and not be answered.

title: A good name over riches
summary: A good reputation is worth more than great wealth, and being well thought of is better than silver or gold.

title: Rich and poor share one Maker
summary: The rich and the poor have this in common: the Lord made them both.

title: Training children for the long run
summary: Shape a child in the path he should take, and as he grows old he tends to keep to it.
note: A general pattern, not a guarantee about how every child will turn out.

title: The generous share their bread
summary: A generous person will be blessed because he shares his food with the poor.

title: Remove the scoffer, end the strife
summary: Drive out a mocker and conflict goes with him; quarreling and insults come to an end.

title: Don't befriend a hothead
summary: Don't make friends with an angry, hot-tempered person, or you'll pick up his ways and trap yourself.

title: Honor your aging parents
summary: Listen to the father who gave you life, don't look down on your mother when she is old, and give your parents reason to rejoice.

title: Don't gloat over an enemy
summary: Don't celebrate when your enemy falls or stumbles, or the Lord will see it, disapprove, and turn his anger away from him.

title: No favorites when judging
summary: Showing partiality in judgment is wrong; whoever declares the guilty innocent is cursed, but those who rebuke wrongdoing will be blessed.

title: Don't testify falsely or pay back
summary: Don't speak against your neighbor without cause or mislead with your words, and don't say you'll do to him what he did to you.

title: Don't grab the place of honor
summary: Don't push yourself forward before the king; it is better to be invited higher than to be sent lower in front of others.

title: Settle it face to face
summary: Don't rush a dispute to court; argue your case with your neighbor directly, and don't betray someone else's confidence, or you'll be shamed.

title: A word at the right time
summary: A word spoken at just the right moment is as beautiful as golden apples set in silver.

title: A rebuke heard well
summary: A wise person's correction, received by a listening ear, is as valuable as gold jewelry.

title: Patience and gentleness persuade
summary: Patience can persuade even a ruler, and a gentle tongue can break through the hardest resistance.

title: Don't sing to a heavy heart
summary: Singing cheerful songs to someone grieving is like taking away his coat on a cold day; it only adds to the hurt.

title: Feed your enemy
summary: Meet your enemy's need for food and water; it will be like burning coals on his head, and the Lord will reward you.

title: When to answer a fool
summary: Don't answer a fool on his own terms or you'll become like him; yet sometimes answer him as his folly deserves, so he doesn't think himself wise.
note: The two sayings sit side by side on purpose; wisdom knows which situation calls for which.

title: Don't meddle in others' fights
summary: Getting involved in a quarrel that isn't yours is like grabbing a stray dog by the ears.

title: Just kidding isn't an excuse
summary: Someone who deceives his neighbor and then says he was only joking is like a madman shooting deadly arrows.

title: Gossip is fuel for conflict
summary: Without wood a fire goes out, and without gossip a quarrel dies down; a quarrelsome person keeps strife burning, and gossip sinks in deep.

title: Let others praise you
summary: Don't sing your own praises; let others, even strangers, do the praising.

title: Faithful wounds from a friend
summary: An open rebuke is better than love that stays hidden; a friend's wounds can be trusted, but an enemy's kisses are many and false.

title: A friend's counsel
summary: A friend's earnest advice is as sweet as perfume; don't abandon your friends or your family's friends, and a neighbor close by beats a brother far away.

title: Sharpening one another
summary: Just as iron hones iron, people sharpen one another through close, honest friendship.

title: Know the state of your flock
summary: Know your flocks well and pay close attention to your herds, because wealth doesn't last.
note: Originally about livestock and wealth; leaders often apply it to knowing the people in their care.

title: Confess and find mercy
summary: Whoever hides his sins won't prosper, but whoever confesses and turns from them finds mercy.

title: Honest rebuke beats flattery
summary: Whoever rebukes someone will end up more appreciated than the person who flatters.

title: Flattery sets a trap
summary: Flattering your neighbor is like spreading a net for his feet.

title: Don't vent all your anger
summary: A fool lets his anger out in full, but a wise person quietly holds it back.

title: Anger breeds conflict
summary: An angry person stirs up conflict, and a hot-tempered one commits many sins.

title: Fear of people is a trap
summary: Fearing what people think or can do is a trap, but whoever trusts in the Lord is kept safe.

title: Stirring anger brings strife
summary: If you've been foolishly proud or plotting harm, cover your mouth; just as churning makes butter, stirring up anger produces strife.

title: Speak up for the voiceless
summary: Speak up for people who can't speak for themselves; judge fairly and defend the rights of the poor and needy.

title: A wife her husband trusts
summary: A wife of strong character is worth more than jewels; her husband trusts her fully, and she does him good, not harm, all her life.

title: Praise at home
summary: Her children call her blessed and her husband praises her, saying she surpasses all others.
